539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a normal rate of 22-25% should be used, with deferred tax rising next year as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar are capitalised; the Q4 deferred tax charge of about Rs 4-4.5 crore related to land recognised as right-of-use assets for the Madhya Bharat project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

risks_watch: Raw-material cost and supply: ammonia and sulphur prices have roughly tripled and remain volatile; management could not predict when they will ease.
Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.
Q1 FY27 inventory-liquidation benefit is unquantified, and management declined to give numbers; also the Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap is unexplained on the call.
Deferred tax and effective tax rate will rise in FY27 as projects capitalise; a term loan may be used for the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat capex.
Governance and disclosure: management relied on the CFO for most figures and its tone on the call was unusually unstructured.
539334|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid but cautious, emphasising conservatism and a wait-and-see stance on Units 5 and 6 and on FY27 pricing. Its visibility was often hedged ("I can't read too far"), and it repeatedly deferred detailed numbers to the CFO or to later IR follow-up.
key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.
Old numbers will never be seen again.
So we will definitely do Rs. 250 crores in that. Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 250 crores.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable and guides Q1 FY27 PAT at 8-8.5% of revenue versus Q4 FY26 PAT margin of 5.8% and FY26 at 7.1%, but sulphur may settle at Rs 70-75/kg versus Rs 30-35/kg earlier and ammonia has risen from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg, so the gain depends on pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Rabi FY27 (after Kharif FY27, roughly H2 FY27)
rows.why: Unit 6 is about 90-95% complete and Unit 5/6 are mechanically ready, but no Kharif FY27 revenue is assumed from them and commissioning is still unscheduled, with trial production only under evaluation and possibly starting within about one month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 chemical volumes rose 27.9% to 72,423 MT and fertiliser sales were 252,777 MT, but FY27 revenue visibility was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore, with existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore assumed from Rabi season.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 65-70%, so there is no capacity-driven case for new capex, but the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat (Unit 3) plan is already on the table and management said it is still looking for a better opportunity and right time to start it, so timing is undated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore and management has not factored in higher current selling prices, so an upgrade would need a clear recovery in dispatches that the call does not show.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue has already been cut once (Rs 1,500 crore to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore), demand is weakening as prices rise, Q4 revenue was flat YoY on chemical volume up 36%, and Unit 5/6 timing is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: after Unit 5/6 commissioning, Rabi FY27 onward
rows.why: Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 chemical plants are mechanically ready but no product launch timing or product names were given on the call.

rows.label: Q1 FY27 inventory liquidation
rows.why: Management said held-back Q4 inventory will be liquidated in Q1 FY27 and guided Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore versus Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 218.2 crore, though it declined to quantify the benefit.

rows.label: NBS subsidy adequacy for fertilisers
rows.why: NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but management says it is still insufficient for current raw-material costs, and a 10% government cap is in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 FY27 PAT margin of 8-8.5% and on Unit 6 being 90-95% complete, but cautious on Units 5/6 start-up, FY27 pricing and the Rs 350 crore Unit 3 project, deferring numbers to the CFO and IR; analysts probed the unexplained Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap and capex funding.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

key_quotes: I believe this year will be much better than the last two or three financial years for the company.
So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.
No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5 %- 9%. I hope so.
Honestly speaking, after these sulfur rates came, we put our acid plants on low load.
First, you need value, then volume.
539334|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on FY27 outlook and pricing, repeatedly calling the year much better than the last two or three. It was evasive on volume recovery and on the Q4-to-Q1 order-slippage question, answering by pointing to revenue and profit growth instead. It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2% in Q1 with gross margin 31.9%; FY27 PAT guided at 8.5-9% (held), with K-acid price up from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus, but sulphur at about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 is a cost headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (Unit 6 trials by end-Aug/Sept 2026); Units 5 and 6
rows.why: Cumulative capex Rs 209 crore of Rs 512 crore spent by 30 June 2026; Unit 6 trials expected end-Aug/Sept giving 4-5 months of FY27 operation, adding to 450,000 MT/yr fertiliser and 72,000 MT/yr chemical capacity across Units 5, 6 and Meghnagar.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q2 FY27 onwards, rising into FY28
rows.why: Q1 volumes fell (fertiliser 66,527 MT vs 76,288 MT, chemicals 9,113 MT vs 14,837 MT), but management expects Q2 to beat Q1, Unit 6 adds 4-5 months of FY27 volume, and FY28 with 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Madhya Bharat project already underway (Rs 60 crore invested to June, 2028 timeline, about twice Unit 6 capacity), Rs 9.3 crore land bought at Lote Parshuram and Rs 125 crore in deposits; utilisation is not disclosed, but acid plants are on low load, so new capacity is not constrained by utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says Q2 will beat Q1 and Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher on Rs 250-285 crore comparison), and that peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices, but this is conditional on Unit 6 trials and volume recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, Q1 chemical volumes fell 39% to 9,113 MT and fertiliser volumes fell 13% to 66,527 MT, and Unit 6 start-up depends on raw material contracts with sulphur at about USD 1,100/t.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said battery-grade phosphoric acid is not on the agenda and the focus is on stabilising current expansions first; the dyes plant (about Rs 37 crore) is already complete, so no new product launch was flagged.

rows.label: K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone inquiries from China
rows.why: Management says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China, while K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus, but no order value was given.

rows.label: Sulphur advance payments and acid plant low load
rows.why: Sulphur requires advance payment at about USD 1,100/t versus USD 250-300 earlier, chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1, and Rs 303 crore of the Rs 512 crore capex is still to be spent, so working-capital strain is likely to persist until acid plants restart.

rows.label: Value-over-volume pricing stance
rows.why: Dispatches were stopped in mid-March 2026 to wait for higher prices, fertiliser inventory is being held, and Q1 revenue rose 10% YoY on volumes down 13% (fertiliser) and 39% (chemicals), so realisations are carrying the top line.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 turnover (Rs 1,250 crore, stretching to Rs 1,350-1,400 crore) and pricing, and cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up and on volume recovery; analysts pushed on the Q4-to-Q1 order slippage, the falling acid-plant load, and guidance that moved between figures.

539334|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 58.2% YoY to INR403.5 crore and EBITDA 87.7% to INR49.2 crore, helped by China-driven dye intermediate demand.
539334|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR403.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 58.2% YoY and 44% QoQ, with H1 at INR683.6 crore (+34.1%). EBITDA rose to INR49.2 crore at a 12.2% margin and PAT to INR35.7 crore at an 8.9% margin. Management attributed the gain to China-driven shortages of dye intermediates, Kharif-season volumes and better realisations, and commissioned Unit 5 (about 6,000 TPA dye capacity) and a 10 MW DC solar plant. The board also approved a INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5 (3,000 TPA, commissioning by March 2028) funded partly by a promoter warrant issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR245 crore (+85% YoY), H1 INR383 crore (+53%). Volume 14,368 MT in Q2 vs about 9,000 MT in Q1; margins lifted by Chinese dye intermediate shortages (H-Acid, vinyl sulfone price spikes).

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR158 crore (+27% YoY), H1 INR300 crore (+15%). Q2 volume about 79,000-80,000 MT; H1 about 1,45,000 MT, roughly 1-1.5% below H1 FY26 per management. Management expects Q3 to be subdued.

guidance_outlook: Management sees FY27 revenue of at least INR1,250 crore and says profitability should be in three digits (INR crore); it calls INR1,250-1,300 crore conservative.
FY28 revenue guided at about INR2,000 crore, with a 10% variation (management also cited INR1,800 crore after 10% depreciation).
Management sees scope for EBITDA and PAT margins to improve 15-20% from current levels over time, but said this is not a FY27 target.
Unit 6 trial production expected around end-Nov/Dec 2026; management is assuming no Unit 6 revenue in Q4 FY27 and full production in FY28.
Q3 FY27 chemical volumes expected to be better than Q2; Q3 fertiliser expected to be subdued due to poor season and pending subsidy announcement.
Long-term: management views current footprint as capable of 2.5-3x today's revenue once all capex completes (personal view, not guidance).
Promoter warrant balance (8,54,060 warrants at INR526.90, about INR45 crore) expected by March 2027, ahead of the June 2027 deadline.
capex_capacity: Unit 5 commercial production commenced in Q2 FY27, adding about 6,000 MT per annum of dye capacity; CFO said Unit 5 adds about 1,500 MT per quarter.
Unit 6 is mechanically complete; raw materials being imported; trial production targeted end-November or December 2026, with 3-3.5 months needed for stabilisation, approvals and NBS subsidy claim.
10 MW DC solar at Nanded commissioned; total consolidated solar capacity 20.6 MW DC.
Madhya Bharat Phosphates (wholly owned, Meghnagar, Jhabua, MP) expansion progressing; INR92 crore invested to 30 Sep 2026, funded entirely by internal accruals.

Board approved INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5, Lote Parshuram: 3,000 MT per annum, commissioning by March 2028. Management estimates about INR250 crore revenue at 75% utilisation but declined to name the product.
Withdrawal of the proposed merger of Kisan and Madhya Bharat from NCLT; management said delays made it unviable.
demand_pricing: Chemical pricing firm on China dye intermediate supply gaps from environmental and safety compliance; management called H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price spikes non-sustainable and said they would normalise over weeks or months.
Management said there was no inventory gain from H-Acid, and sulfur prices are starting to ease.
Fertiliser demand supported by availability in drought-affected Maharashtra and MP; about 79,000 MT sold in Q2 despite poor rains. Central subsidy rate not yet declared (expected around 5 November).
Acid complex still running at lower levels because sulfur was high-priced and sulfuric acid could not be sold profitably.
Customer demand recovering gradually after earlier wait-and-watch; management said global demand is still somewhat weak.
Management said receivables were reviewed and are fine; realisations have risen (e.g., INR100 product now selling at INR103-110).

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 to Q2 growth between volume and realisation, and impact of global conflict.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain was a mix of volume (Kharif peak) and realisation, with margins helped by Chinese dye intermediate shortages; Q3 fertiliser to be subdued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 chemical sales (INR245 crore) was opportunistic from H-Acid, and what are margin prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price hikes are not a major driver and are not sustainable; it sees EBITDA and PAT margins better than current levels over time, but declined to quantify FY27 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoter warrant money come in, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance warrant money expected before March 2027, against a June 2027 deadline, to fund Madhya Bharat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall and was there an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin fell from 32% in Q1 to 30% in Q2 (33% in Q2 FY26), attributed to inventory level changes; management denied any inventory gain.

qa_highlights.question: Next-year revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 revenue should be near INR2,000 crore, with about 10% variation, while FY27 is at least INR1,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Kisan-Madhya Bharat merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: NCLT delays made the merger overtaken by events, so management withdrew the application as a conscious decision.

risks_watch: Chemical margins rest on temporary China-driven price spikes in H-Acid and vinyl sulfone; management itself expects normalisation.
Fertiliser H2 subdued by poor monsoon, El Nino and a pending central subsidy rate; Q3 expected weaker.
Unit 6 revenue timing uncertain: trial in Dec 2026, stabilisation and NBS/PDIL approvals may push revenue into FY28.
Management declined to disclose the product or economics of the INR70 crore Unit 5 project, and the capex-per-tonne versus Unit 5's INR37 crore raised questions.
Receivables rising and gross margin dipping QoQ were questioned; the CFO's explanation was limited.
Promoter warrant funding of about INR45 crore is pending shareholder and other approvals and is due by June 2027.
Monitor Q3 FY27 chemical volumes (management expects above 14,368 MT) and the FY27 INR1,250 crore run-rate.
539334|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the headline numbers and FY28 ambition, but guarded and deflecting on H-Acid pricing sustainability, product details of new capex, gross margin drivers and Unit 6 timing. Management repeatedly stressed being conservative while also voicing aggressive long-term targets.
key_quotes: So first of all, the margins have improved because of good demand from China in all these products.
In my opinion, if you ask me, we should be able to achieve at least INR1,250 crores of total sales and profitability should be in three digits.
Sir, if I talk about next year, like 2027-2028, in my opinion, we should be somewhere closer to near around INR2,000 crores.
Sulfur is starting to come down, and there was no inventory gain, sir.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The INR1,334.61 crore trading EBIT includes one-offs, so the recurring run rate may be lower (about INR1,000-1,100 crore per management); also watch intersegment transfer pricing, which shifts profit between trading and CGD.
The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.

Cash and other financial assets are unclear: management cited about INR5,000 crore cash, while the balance sheet shows about INR1,300 crore cash plus about INR5,500 crore other financial assets, including GSFS-placed funds. The company will provide a breakup.
Watch Q1 FY27 results (early August 2026) for the first post-merger quarter and EBITDA by segment.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.

CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.
Management said spot prices near $20/mmBtu make gas costlier than propane, so volume recovery is unlikely near term.
Gas trading sourcing: about 20% long-term (Brent-linked, of which about 20% Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic, about 67% spot.
Gas trading margin: fertilizer marketing margin is fixed at about INR20/scm; industrial margins are market-driven. Management said there will be no negative trading quarters.
Morbi volume rose from about 0.4 mmscmd in April 2026 to about 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the Morbi cluster up 181% vs Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

risks_watch: Morbi volume sustainability: run-rate about 3 mmscmd versus 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts and propane supply recovering.

Gas trading margin durability: Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores against FY27 guidance of about INR1,100 crores, with management stating it is conservative; Q2 visibility limited by Middle East volatility.
CGD EBITDA below guidance at INR5.18/scm against the INR5.5-6.5/scm range; management kept guidance but gave no segment-level explanation.
Third-party gas trading volumes down to about 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, with recovery expected only in FY28-29.
Power segment utilisation very low (about 6% PLF at GSEG and 1% at Pipavav); revival strategy to be shared in a few months.

Our focus remains clear to maintain the right balance between volume growth and sustainable margins while continuing to serve our customers reliably and efficiently.
No, there will not be any negative numbers. I think we stick to our guidance last time we gave around INR1,100 crores of profit from the gas trading business.
We expect this towards early September.

539336|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59% YoY to INR9,826 crore and EBITDA 20% to INR1,019 crore, while Morbi demand fell from ~8 to ~3.8 MMSCMD.

Gas trading margin fell to about 4% in Q2 from a higher Q1, attributed to force majeure disruption of Qatar LNG volumes requiring spot replacement. Management is securing 0.8 MTPA of long-term LNG (Henry Hub-linked, deliveries from 2028) to compete with propane for Morbi demand, which normalised sharply in Q2.

segments.name: City gas distribution (CGD)

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Q2 CNG volumes 3.67 MMSCMD (+11% YoY); H1 at 3.72 MMSCMD. Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%. 18 stations added in H1, taking the total to 857; target 75+ additions in FY27.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7,615 crore in Q2 (+84% YoY) and EBITDA INR329 crore (+89% YoY). Gross trading margin about 4% in Q2 vs higher in Q1; management reiterated 5-6% guidance for the rest of FY27. Trading sourced 12.31 MMSCMD, of which 4.67 MMSCMD sold externally and 7.63 MMSCMD to CGD.

539359|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.

Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?

qa_highlights.question: Why has the detailed margin roadmap (13% to 17%) not been published, and what is the CCC outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported EBITDA target of about 14% by FY29 stands, but priorities have shifted to quarterly delivery after the March 2026 environment change. Cash conversion cycle is about 140 days and expected to persist until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 35 crore low-margin exit hurt FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing strong demand and early indications in the first 45 days of Q1; European growth is expected to accelerate with the Almere plant.

risks_watch: Raw-material and crude-linked cost inflation has not yet fully flowed through; management expects pressure in coming quarters despite pricing actions.
Gross debt is expected to rise in the next 3-6 months due to inventory build, and insurance receipts after the fire may lag capex.
Start-up losses of about Rs 80-85 crore a year from US, UK and Germany development centres continue until revenue ramps (about 3 years).
Supplier contract honouring in flavours and raw material availability over the next 2-3 months.
Management did not give full-year FY27 guidance and deferred the detailed margin roadmap.
539450|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on H1 FY27 margin and pricing visibility, but cautious and non-committal beyond H1 due to raw-material and inflation uncertainty. Management was candid about the Rs 35 crore one-off and the reported margin gap, and it deferred the detailed three-year margin plan.
key_quotes: So, as we have given our guidance and even if you look at the fourth quarter this year, we are at 13% and something adjusted EBITDA from the sustainable operating business.
We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary.
Our key objective remains clear, protecting margins while ensuring supply security for our customers.
I am actually confident that we will hit the Rs. 300 crore plus EBITDA for this year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: H1 FY27 hold, then FY27-FY29 path
rows.why: Management guides adjusted EBITDA margin ~13-13.5% through H1 FY27 (Q4 FY26 adj. 13.5%), with reported margin at 10.2% in FY26 and target 14% by FY29; raw-material inventory prices up 12-13%+ are not yet in Q4 numbers, so expansion above current levels is conditional on pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Vanavate around Q1 FY27 end; Vashivali around Q3 FY27
rows.why: Vanavate facility expected on stream around end of the current quarter with a six-month transition from Mulund, and Vashivali rebuild may be available around Q3 FY27; Almere in Netherlands already fully operational with about Rs 10 crore annual sales transferred, and Europe near full utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management cites rapid flavours volume growth, share gains during inflation as smaller players hold less inventory, Q1 FY27 secured on price and supply, and rest-of-world sales up about 34% YoY in Q4, though full-year revenue guidance was withheld.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at about Rs 140 crore, mostly front-loaded in H1, with management saying no large India capex is planned apart from the fire-related rebuild; no new utilisation figure disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined full-year FY27 revenue or margin guidance beyond H1 citing raw-material uncertainty, and holds the Rs 300 crore-plus FY27 EBITDA target rather than raising it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material and crude-linked inflation (inventory prices up 12-13%+, about 40% of RM crude-linked) has not yet hit Q4 and management says pressure will show in coming quarters, with Q2 margin 'subject to monitoring' and a 12-13% floor.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or molecule launches were discussed.

rows.label: US and UK development centres ramp (Rs 80-85 crore annual opex, ~3-year break-ev
rows.when: 3-4 year ramp, start-up losses through FY27-FY29
rows.why: US business of about 1 million (about 200,000 already in hand) is contracted and Manchester started this year, but new centres take about 3 years to break even and carry Rs 80-85 crore annual opex across three centres.

rows.label: Contracted US business and Middle East/SE Asia growth
rows.why: Contracted US business of about 1 million with about 200,000 already in hand; rest-of-world Q4 sales up about 34% YoY per analyst question; Southeast Asia factory at break-even.

rows.label: Gross debt to rise before falling
rows.when: next 3-6 months, then 10% annual reduction long term
rows.why: Borrowings guided around Rs 800 crore in FY27 versus gross debt of Rs 851 crore at end-March 2026, with inventory build and insurance receipts lagging the fire-related capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 FY27 margin (~13-13.5%) and pricing pass-through and the Rs 300 crore-plus FY27 EBITDA target, but cautious beyond H1 on raw-material inflation and withheld full-year guidance and the detailed margin roadmap; analysts pushed on the returns from the Rs 350 crore capex a

539450|2026-06.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.
539450|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore and EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 89 crore, with margin expanding to 13.4% from 12.6%. Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. Global Ingredients was softer on supply gaps, and Fragrances India was flat as the company exited low-margin business and repriced clients. Net debt rose Rs 65 crore to Rs 852 crore on inventory build and capex, and a Rs 30 crore insurance exceptional item was booked.

financial_highlights.change: Supported by product mix and raw material planning
Normalised about Rs 95-96 crore excluding about Rs 15 crore pre-ordering
Expected to rise to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate capitalisation

segments.name: Flavours
segments.commentary: Strong broad-based growth; Rs 112 crore in Q1 versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore attributed to pre-ordering and extra channel stock. Management expects Q2 to be above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore.

segments.name: Fragrances (Europe and international)
segments.commentary: Healthy growth led by Europe and select international markets. Europe plant operational since May; European capex completed. Segment margins are weighed down by higher R&D and global CDC opex.

segments.name: Fragrances India
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, against a strong Q1 FY26 base. Company exited low-margin business and held back shipments until price corrections were agreed; about 95% of clients accepted price increases.

segments.name: Global Ingredients
segments.commentary: Softer quarter on lower demand in select export markets and supply gaps from raw-material constraints; management expects recovery in H2.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for full FY27, but would not give a precise full-year margin range beyond the next 2-3 months.
If double-digit growth holds, EBITDA in absolute terms should be similar to Q1 levels; margin could vary about 1% either way.
Raw material costs said to be fixed for about 6 months via stock in hand and contracts; about 45 days extra inventory built to pass on future cost shocks.
Net debt expected broadly flat at June level through Q2 (may rise slightly in September), then fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3.
Remaining India capex about Rs 100 crore in total (Rs 25 crore in Q1 done, Rs 25 crore in Q2 on Vanvate, about Rs 50 crore for the three India plants); Vanvate factory commissioning in Q3.
Target ETR below 30%, from 31.5-32% currently.
Long-term targets: ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years and 20% long term; European business ROCE 17-18% over the long run.
US revenue expected at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27; UK business needs 12-15 months before material revenue.
capex_capacity: Europe capex of about Rs 25 crore in Q1 completed; Almere factory operational since May 2026 and a large R&D centre in Germany added.
India: Vanvate factory to be commissioned in Q3 FY27; bulk of India investment capex expected by end of Q2.
Vashivali plant upgrade: last Rs 25 crore may be spent in Q4 FY27 or deferred to Q1 FY28, depending on demand.
Extra R&D spend of about USD 3 million a year in Europe.
Quarterly depreciation about Rs 35 crore, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate capitalisation.
demand_pricing: Price corrections passed to about 95%+ of clients after raw-material cost inflation linked to West Asia geopolitics; clients reluctant to accept were not supplied until negotiations concluded.
Flavours pre-ordering of 1-2 to 3 weeks was driven by long lead and shipping times; July momentum reported as steady.
Global Ingredients supply curtailed due to raw-material uncertainty; backward integration and China de-risking steps said to be in place.
Unilever and global accounts: ongoing project flow but no large new breakthroughs; Unilever's own pricing pressures and weak India launches noted.
Management cites a US plus UK fragrance market of about USD 10 billion, roughly 4-5x India's fragrance market, with about USD 100 million addressable in the near term.
Around 10-11% of revenue comes from products launched in the last 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year Flavours budget and how much did FX add to revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Flavours was Rs 112 crore versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore pulled forward. Like-for-like growth was about 9%, and FX added about 5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is flat India Fragrance a high-base effect, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was strong. The company deliberately exited low-margin business, held back shipments during price negotiations, and says it now services almost all clients after building inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be guided for FY27, and is the Q1 gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise full-year range was given. Management says Q1 is a normal quarter, not exceptional, so EBITDA should be similar in absolute terms if double-digit growth continues, with margin varying about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the factory timelines, debt path and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Vanvate commissions in Q3. Debt stays near June levels, then falls about Rs 25 crore a quarter from Q3. ETR is 31.5-32% now, targeted below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe ramp-up and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Germany is expected to break even in FY27 or FY28, the US a year later, and the UK a year after that. Long-term European ROCE is 17-18%, and group ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years, rising to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance claim status and how is depreciation trending?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 30 crore was received in Q1, with Rs 50-60 crore still pending and full settlement expected in FY27. Depreciation is about Rs 35 crore a quarter, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate.

risks_watch: Flavours Q1 (Rs 112 crore) includes about Rs 15 crore of pre-ordering and extra channel stock that management says will not recur every quarter; Q2 is guided above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore

Raw material cost visibility of about 6 months from July, backed by stock in hand, contracts and about 45 days of extra inventory; cost shocks beyond that could hit gross margin if prices cannot be passed on
Global Ingredients softness from supply gaps and lower export demand; recovery is expected only in H2 FY27
Fragrances India flat YoY after deliberate exit from low-margin business and shipment holds; watch whether volumes recover as price increases settle

Net debt of Rs 852 crore expected to stay near June level through Q2 (may rise in September), with reduction of about Rs 25 crore per quarter only from Q3; Rs 50-60 crore of insurance claim still pending

Europe and India capex ramp: Vanvate commissioning in Q3 FY27, Europe losses expected to persist until breakeven in FY27-FY28 (Germany), with US and UK following a year apart; effective tax rate is 31.5-32% against a target below 30%
key_quotes: So, we have prepared in a manner that we have 6 months visibility on the inventory and our contracts or pricing to the client.
But for the full year, we are not confident to predict beyond 2, 3 months' time.
This is the baseline normal quarter.
We do not expect Rs. 112 plus growth in the quarter 2. That is not our expectation.
539450|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious and guarded on the outlook: management calls Q1 a normal quarter but declines to give a full-year margin range beyond 2-3 months, citing geopolitical volatility, energy and freight costs. Confident on near-term execution points such as raw material cover, Europe plant commissioning and supply continuity for existing clients.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 13.4% from 12.6% (about 80 bps), but Q1 included about Rs 15 crore of Flavours pre-ordering, and management gave no precise full-year margin range; margin could vary about 1% either way with EBITDA similar to Q1 (~Rs 89 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vanvate factory in India is guided for commissioning in Q3 FY27 with about Rs 25 crore capex in Q2, and Almere (Europe) went live in May 2026; depreciation rises from about Rs 35 crore to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates double-digit FY27 revenue growth (Q1 +14% reported, ~9% like-for-like, FX ~5 pts), with Flavours normalised at Rs 95-96 crore and Q2 guided above that, and Global Ingredients expected to recover in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Remaining India capex is about Rs 100 crore (Rs 25 crore done in Q1, Rs 25 crore Q2, about Rs 50 crore for three plants) with Vashivali's last Rs 25 crore possibly deferred to Q1 FY28; no new capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guarded, declining a full-year margin range beyond 2-3 months and citing geopolitical, energy and freight volatility, while Q1 was flattered by about Rs 15 crore of pre-ordering.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 Flavours is guided above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore, Global Ingredients is supply-constrained until H2, and raw-material cover is only about 6 months, so a cost shock beyond that could hit gross margin.

rows.label: Net debt reduction from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Net debt of Rs 852 crore is guided flat through Q2, then to fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3; Rs 50-60 crore of insurance claim is still pending.

rows.label: Effective tax rate reduction to below 30%
rows.why: ETR is 31.5-32% in Q1 against a stated target below 30%, but no timing or driver for the cut was given.

rows.label: Europe breakeven ramp (Germany, US, UK)
rows.when: Germany FY27 or FY28; US a year later; UK a year after that
rows.why: Almere is operational since May 2026 and European capex is complete, with US revenue guided at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27 and UK needing 12-15 months before material revenue; European losses persist until breakeven.

tone.note: Management was confident on raw-material cover, Europe commissioning and client supply continuity, but cautious on full-year margins, Global Ingredients and geopolitical cost risk; analysts pushed on the Flavours pre-ordering one-off, the margin outlook and the debt path.

539450|2026-09.headline: S H Kelkar H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% to Rs.1,299 crore and EBITDA 33% to Rs.168 crore, with margin at 13%.
539450|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 15% YoY to Rs.636 crore, and H1 revenue reached Rs.1,299 crore (up 14%). H1 EBITDA rose 33% to Rs.168 crore, margin about 13%, with gross margins broadly stable despite raw material volatility. Flavour revenue grew 47% in H1 to Rs.184 crore, though management called part of Q1 a one-off inventory build by customers. Net debt stood at Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026, which management expects to be the peak for the year as inventory is reduced.

segments.name: Fragrance
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.1,088 crore, up 11.9% YoY; management cites about 14% underlying growth excluding roughly Rs.50 crore of low-margin business hived off in Q4 FY26. Domestic growth about 9% (roughly 5% price, 4% volume).

segments.name: Flavour
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.184 crore, up 47% YoY; Q2 revenue about Rs.72 crore versus a Q1 that was higher. Management sees Rs.90 crore per quarter as the run rate and about 20% sustainable growth.

segments.name: Overseas CDCs (Germany, UK, US)
segments.commentary: First sales achieved in all three markets; revenue is small and management says it will take 12-18 months to become meaningful. Around Rs.80 crore of spend in these centres is not yet generating meaningful revenue.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 12-13% per year on a continuing basis over the next 2-3 years, with EBITDA growth of 13-14% per year.
Gross margin expected in the 43% range; upside of about 0.5% if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease.
EBITDA margin of 15%+ targeted within 12-18 months at steady-state inflation, or about two years if inflation persists; 13% described as the lower end of sustainable.
Interest cost expected at Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A expected at Rs.145-150 crore annualised after new facility capitalisation.
Net debt expected to fall from September 2026 peak by March 2027; insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.
Remaining FY27 capex about Rs.30-35 crore; FY28 capex about Rs.75-80 crore including spillover, with maintenance capex about Rs.15 crore.
capex_capacity: Europe capex almost complete; Europe factory operational since May 2026 and fully operational in Q2.
India Fragrance factory renewal expected to be completed and put to use in Q4 FY27; transition from Mulund follows in FY28.
Second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) expected to be put to use in Q4 FY28, concluding the large expansion.
Jakarta (Southeast Asia) factory in full operation since September 2025, improving lead times to clients.
Overseas development centres in Germany, Manchester (UK) and US are fully staffed and in use; no further CDC investment planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic Fragrance growth split roughly 5% price and 4% volume; large clients are growing faster than smaller clients, which management calls transient.
Excluding about Rs.25 crore of intentionally exited low-margin categories, like-for-like growth is about 12%.
Management expects a stabilisation in raw material prices and strong H2 demand, but flagged the Middle East situation as the biggest risk.
Flavour growth in Q1 was partly a one-off as customers built inventory due to freight and logistics disruption; management expects about 20% sustainable growth.
More than 5,000 clients served globally; no specific RFQs cited. Europe and US smaller-brand and mid-size opportunities are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fragrance growth split between volume and value in domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 5% from price and 4% from volume in the domestic Fragrance business, which grew about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: When will inventory unwind and working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory reduction started in October 2026; management does not expect a sharp total inventory fall but expects lower inventory intensity as sales grow over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable interest and depreciation run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A about Rs.145-150 crore annualised, with European acquisition amortisation reducing from 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Flavour Q2 run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 at about Rs.72 crore was below the normal run rate and Rs.90 crore per quarter is the right run rate; Q1 was above it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE below 12% since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature India businesses earn about 20% ROCE; overseas investment, the 2024 expansion and fire-related domestic capex weigh on the figure. Rs.80 crore of CDC spend is not yet earning returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone margin low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and should recover once operations move back next year.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, raw material inflation and availability, and geopolitical outcomes after the US midterm elections.
Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 2026 and working capital tied up in high inventory; delivery on the March 2027 reduction target.
Flavour growth lumpiness from customer order timing and inventory destocking after Q1 one-off demand.
Overseas CDCs take 12-18 months to become meaningful; ROCE remains below 12% in the near term.
Execution of Fragrance factory renewal (Q4 FY27) and second factory (Q4 FY28) with capex spillover into FY28.
539450|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term inflation and geopolitics; management repeatedly declined to extrapolate the 40%+ Flavour growth and reset the base to about 20%.
key_quotes: We expect September debt level to represent a peak for the year with the reduction anticipated by March 2027 as we optimize inventory levels.
So, we expect 14% on a 12% revenue growth, 13% to 14% EBITDA growth year-on-year in the next 2-3 years.

It will take a good three to four years before we are breakeven in those markets by themselves and then another further three to four years as we continue to grow to generate meaningful returns on this investment.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 15%+ EBITDA margin in 12-18 months at steady inflation, from H1 FY27 margin of about 13%, with gross margin held in the 43% range and upside of about 0.5% if raw material conditions ease.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Europe factory is already operational (fully in Q2 FY27), India Fragrance factory renewal is due Q4 FY27 and the second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) is due Q4 FY28, though the second factory timing sits beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance is 12-13% continuing revenue growth per year, with domestic Fragrance volume at about 4% and Flavour run rate seen at Rs.90 crore per quarter with about 20% sustainable growth, but no firm RFQs or order book were cited.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Remaining FY27 capex is only about Rs.30-35 crore and FY28 capex of about Rs.75-80 crore is already planned, with CDC investment finished and no further CDC investment planned; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management could benefit if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease, which would add about 0.5% to the 43% gross margin, but the guide is held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged the Middle East conflict and raw material inflation as the biggest risks, and Flavour growth is lumpy after Q1 inventory build, with Q2 at about Rs.72 crore below the Rs.90 crore run rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Net debt peak and inventory unwind
rows.why: Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026 is expected to be the peak, with inventory reduction starting October 2026 and insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.

rows.label: Overseas CDCs becoming meaningful
rows.why: First sales achieved in Germany, UK and US, but Rs.80 crore of CDC spend is not yet generating meaningful revenue and management says it takes 12-18 months, so ROCE stays below 12% near term.

rows.label: Standalone margin recovery after fire
rows.why: Operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and are expected to recover once operations move back, with Mulund transition in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on 12-13% medium-term growth and a 15%+ EBITDA margin in 12-18 months, but cautious on near-term inflation, the Middle East and the one-off Flavour Q1 build; analysts focused on the volume versus price split, the Flavour run rate and the ROCE below 12%.

539523|2026-03.headline: Alkem Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.6% YoY to INR36,033 million and FY26 EBITDA crossed INR3,000 crore, with management guiding FY27 margins to 20-21%.
539523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR36,033 million (+14.6% YoY), with India sales up 8.8% to INR23,245 million and international sales up 25.4% to INR12,223 million. Q4 EBITDA was INR5,174 million at a 14.4% margin, and FY26 EBITDA grew 32.2% YoY per management, with a 20.4% full-year margin. Q4 net profit was INR2,365 million after exceptional items of INR602.7 million (labour code gratuity/leave liability) and INR747 million (real estate impairment). Management flagged rising logistics, API and packaging costs from geopolitical disruption, and announced that CEO Dr. Vikas Gupta is leaving; a new CEO search is underway.

financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 12.4% in Q4 FY25 (as stated)

financial_highlights.value: INR3,052 million per slide (management also said crossed INR3,000 crore); margin 20.4%
financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 19.4% in FY25; EBITDA +19.6% YoY (stated), +32.2% (stated for Q4 context)

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 India sales grew 8.8% YoY to INR23,245 million; management said branded generics grew close to 10%. IQVIA shows Q4 growth of 11.1% vs IPM ~10%, with chronic +16.1% vs IPM 13.6% and acute +10% vs IPM 7.7%.

segments.name: International (US and ROW)
segments.commentary: Q4 international sales rose 25.4% YoY to INR12,223 million; FY26 international sales were INR4,610 million (+22.5%). Management did not split US and ROW figures for the quarter.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 trade generics growth was about 4.3% on an annualised basis after the carve-out into a separate entity; management is prioritising margin over top-line.

segments.name: Enzene (CDMO/biologics)
segments.commentary: Enzene India is at a high-teens EBITDA margin; Enzene US is loss-making during ramp-up and the group is not expected to be EBITDA positive this year. US CDMO revenue was under INR100 crore last year.

segments.name: Medtech (Occlutech)
segments.commentary: Medtech contributes less than 1% of revenue today. Occlutech acquisition expected to close in 45-60 days.

guidance_outlook: India: grow 100-150 bps above the market; with the market growing ~9-10%, management called double-digit growth the target.
US (dollar terms): high single-digit growth on pharma, plus forex gain and new launches; Tolvaptan launch expected around Sep/Oct 2026 with limited competition.
ROW: higher-teens growth assumed for FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin: 20-21% range (like-to-like), subject to geopolitical and cost clarity; management said it will know more by H2 or Q3.
R&D spend expected at 4-5% of revenue annually; Q4 runs higher (6-6.5%) because of filing cycle.
Other expenses expected to rise 7-8% in FY27, excluding the Occlutech acquisition.
Tax rate guided down to 27-29% from FY27 after moving to the new tax regime from April 2026 (previously 35-38%).
Dividend: 25-30% of PAT currently; management does not foresee a major cut in absolute dividend, so the payout ratio will rise as PAT rises.
capex_capacity: Enzene US biologics plant recently commissioned; ramp-up ongoing, no clear evidence yet of onetime asset turnover from US in-sourcing trend.
No further acquisitions planned for at least 12 months; Occlutech integration into Alkem MedTech expected to take about 12 months after closing.
Denosumab (Prolia/Xgeva) biosimilar under US FDA review; US launch not expected this year, possibly out-licensed.
Semaglutide: injectable approved and launched in India in March 2026; oral tablet in clinical trials; US filing planned in about 1.5 years.
demand_pricing: Q4 chronic branded generic growth 16.1% vs IPM 13.6%; outperformed in 6 key therapies: GI, vitamins and minerals, pain, antidiabetic, respiratory and dermatology.
Chronic is about 22% of India branded generics, up roughly 1 percentage point a year over 3-4 years.
Semaglutide launched day 1 in March 2026; about 11% unit market share in the latest IQVIA report.
Anti-infective market (oral liquids and injectables) remains muted; management said Alkem's acute growth is still high single-digit.
Domestic field force around 14,500 MRs at group level; attrition 18-19%.
Geopolitical environment has raised logistics, API and packaging costs; management hedges 80% of forex exposure and buys API and packaging inventory on price dips.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for India growth and the margin path given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: India is targeted at 100-150 bps above the market; FY26 margin of 20.4% is the baseline and FY27 is seen at 20-21%, with 100 bps annual expansion now a moving target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech deal timing and the impact on numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Deal expected to close in 45-60 days; if it closes, Q2 FY27 would carry a full quarter impact. Medtech is under 1% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Denosumab biosimilar timeline in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: US approval is possibly by Q1 CY27 subject to inspection; no launch this year. Europe has one partner for the Prolia biosimilar; the Xgeva version has no partner yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CEO succession and CXO plan?
qa_highlights.answer: A new CEO will be hired from top global candidates, taking a few months. Non-pharma group businesses (Occlutech, Enzene) report to other promoters or the MD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan launch and expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch expected around September or October 2026 as a limited-player launch, so contribution comes in H2 FY27; base US business faces value erosion.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for dividend and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 25-30% of PAT; absolute payout is expected to be maintained, so the payout percentage will rise after the tax reset. No acquisitions for 12 months.

Denosumab US approval and Europe partnering timing; Tolvaptan launch in Sep/Oct 2026.
Trade generics receivables risk and weak growth in FY26 (about 4.3%).
Enzene US ramp-up losses and CDMO revenue, which is expected to take a couple of years to reach INR200-300 crore.

539523|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on domestic execution and chronic/semaglutide momentum, but cautious on FY27 margins and cost inflation, with management repeatedly declining to quantify headwinds. Tone is measured on the US and Enzene timelines, which management says will take time.
key_quotes: We are confident that with our strong capabilities and adequate inventory built up, we are well positioned to mitigate the potential disruptions and ensure continuity of operations.
In the current scenario, it's a moving goalpost.
we don't foresee any major reduction in absolute value of dividend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed as a plan and no utilisation figure was given; the call instead emphasises acquisitions (Occlutech) and Enzene ramp-up, with no new capex or capacity guided and no acquisitions planned for 12 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on India chronic outperformance (+16.1% vs IPM 13.6%) and Semaglutide (~11% unit share in latest IQVIA), but guidance will only be firmed up once geopolitical and cost clarity arrives in H2 or Q3.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
