rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Tolvaptan Sep/Oct 2026; Denosumab US approval possibly by Q1
rows.why: Tolvaptan US launch guided for around Sep/Oct 2026 as a limited-player launch, contributing in H2 FY27; Denosumab biosimilar US launch not expected this year and may be out-licensed, while Semaglutide oral filing is ~1.5 years away.

rows.label: Occlutech acquisition closing
rows.when: Within 45-60 days of call; full impact from Q2 FY27
rows.why: Deal expected to close in 45-60 days, and if it closes Q2 FY27 carries a full quarter impact, though Medtech is under 1% of revenue today so the numerical effect is small.

rows.label: Enzene US ramp-up and CDMO revenue
rows.when: Couple of years to reach INR200-300 crore; group not EBITDA
rows.why: Enzene US is loss-making during ramp-up, Enzene India runs at high-teens EBITDA margin, and US CDMO revenue was under INR100 crore last year, so the drag persists through FY27.

rows.label: Tax rate reset and dividend payout
rows.why: Tax rate guided down to 27-29% from 35-38% after moving to the new regime from April 2026, and absolute dividend is held so the 25-30% payout ratio will rise as PAT rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on India chronic outperformance, Semaglutide launch and the tax reset, but cautious on FY27 margins and cost inflation, repeatedly declining to quantify headwinds; analysts pushed on margin path, CEO succession and Denosumab/Tolvaptan timing.

539523|2026-06.headline: Alkem Q1 FY27 revenue rose close to 11% to INR3,740 crores, but net profit fell 21.7% on tax, and the Daman US plant received an OAI status.
539523|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR3,740 crores, up close to 11% YoY, with India at INR2,497 crores (+10.3%) and international at INR1,222 crores (+16%). EBITDA margin was 20.5% (EBITDA up 3.7% YoY), PBT was up about 1.8%, and net profit fell 21.7%, which management attributed to tax. Trade Generics was flat YoY in April-June, which dragged India growth, while branded generics grew about 12%. The Daman facility received an OAI status from the USFDA, which management says has not interrupted supplies.

financial_highlights.value: Improved QoQ and YoY, not quantified

segments.name: India formulations - Trade Generics
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; drag due to tighter receivables/DSO practices, API-linked price increases and competition. Management says it is number 1 or 2 in the segment.

segments.name: India formulations - Branded / non-trade (ex-Trade Generics)
segments.commentary: Branded generics grew about 12%; price up about 6%, new launches about 3%, volume about 2%. Chronic grew 17.9% vs IPM 15.4%; acute grew 12.3% vs IPM 10.1%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,222 crores, +16% YoY. Management cites Chile, Australia and small high-growth markets such as Germany (35-40% growth) as drivers.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Management described US as challenging with little volume growth and near-flat price erosion; FY27 US guidance now high single digit to mid, helped by currency. Daman plant supplies about 45% of US revenue.

segments.name: MedTech (Occlutech and ortho)
segments.commentary: Occlutech acquisition completed mid-July, so no Q1 impact; ex-diligence, Q1 EBITDA loss of about INR5-7 crores from ortho/MedTech. FY27 target about INR400 crores sales for the roughly 8.5 months of ownership with breakeven EBITDA.

segments.name: US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs)
segments.commentary: Operating cost about INR60 crores per quarter; breakeven needs about USD25-30 million annualised revenue, now expected in FY28, with capex needed later and no US FDA approval yet on the facility.

guidance_outlook: US revenue growth now guided at high single digit to mid for FY27, versus earlier high single digit, with currency support.
India growth for the full year about 1 percentage point better than the prior guidance, which management put at close to 12%.
Gross margin guidance of 66.5%-67% maintained for the balance of FY27, with API price increases expected to weigh in later quarters.
Consolidated tax rate guided at 30%-32% (standalone earlier 27%-28%), because loss-making entities such as US Enzene carry no deferred tax asset.
Occlutech FY27 target about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA; EBITDA margin improving 7-8% YoY and reaching guidance over 3-4 years.
US CDMO expected to break even in 4-5 quarters per CFO, but MD later said it will not break even within 12 months; Trade Generics growth expected to recover to late single digits.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delayed by at least a few months; Xgeva biosimilar EU launch about 3 months away; Tolvaptan US generic launch expected this quarter.
capex_capacity: Daman US facility received OAI status; corrective and preventive actions initiated, resolution expected in 6-12 months; 45% of US revenue comes from Daman.

Enzene US CDMO (mAbs, development to clinical supplies) operational since November 2025; capacity described as small but technologically differentiated; not yet US FDA approved; capex will be needed later, not this year.
Added about 1,200 MRs over the last few quarters, adding to employee cost.
Backward integration into 7 biosimilars in India generating about INR150 crores annual sales, with improved margins.
Acquisition of Occlutech completed mid-July 2026; integration started, with more India-operations integration expected from next quarter.
demand_pricing: India Trade Generics competition has intensified as large players entered; company also tightened receivable days, slowing primary sales.
Price in India ex-Trade Generics up about 6% YoY; US price erosion close to flat, which management says may have bottomed out.
Semaglutide going off patent is driving chronic market growth; Alkem's benefit so far is very small.
Gross margin improved on lower Trade Generics mix, stronger prescription business and currency; API price increases will weigh on later quarters.
Outperformed IPM in 7 focus therapies: anti-infectives 1.1x, gastro 1.2x, vitamins and minerals 1.4x, pain 1.8x, antidiabetic 1.4x, respiratory 1.6x, derma 1.6x.
Five US ANDA approvals in the quarter, one of them tentative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India growth (10.3%) below most peers, and will it ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drag to Trade Generics, which was flat to mildly up; branded generics grew about 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase is from CDMO and MedTech, and what are the losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose more than 16% from increments, about 1,200 added MRs and Enzene CDMO becoming operational in November 2025; US CDMO opex is about INR60 crores per quarter; ex-Occlutech MedTech losses are about INR5-7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Trade Generics outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was flat in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; management expects recovery, and personally would be happy with late single digits over the next 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech outlook and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target of about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA for about 8.5 months; the earlier 10% margin guidance is pushed out, reaching guidance over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of US revenue depends on the Daman plant, and are supplies affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Daman accounts for about 45% of US revenue; management says supplies continue without interruption and the impact is not expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and US outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated tax rate is 30-32% because loss-making entities carry no deferred tax asset; US growth guided at high single digit to mid, helped by currency and not volume.

risks_watch: Daman OAI status: resolution timeline 6-12 months, and whether it affects US supplies or new ANDA approvals; company has 45% of US revenue from this plant.
Trade Generics: whether growth recovers to late single digits as receivables discipline and API-driven price rises play out.
API price increases pressuring gross margin in the coming quarters against the 66.5%-67% guidance.
US CDMO: lumpy contract timing, USD25-30 million annualised breakeven, and FY28 revenue timeline.
Net profit fall of 21.7% and the 30-32% consolidated tax rate; watch for deferred tax asset recognition.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delay; CEO hire still pending.
539523|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on India branded and international growth, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Trade Generics, US CDMO timelines and the Daman OAI, where answers were often qualified or deferred.
key_quotes: While this represents an important regulatory development, approved product supplies from the facility continue to the U.S. market without any interruption.

rows.why: Enzene CDMO capex needed later, not this year, with breakeven at USD25-30 million annualised revenue now expected in FY28; utilisation not disclosed so no clear high-utilisation trigger.

rows.why: US growth already cut to high single digit to mid, Trade Generics flat YoY in April-June, and API price increases to weigh on later-quarter gross margin against the 66.5%-67% guide; Daman OAI resolution takes 6-12 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tolvaptan US generic launch guided this quarter, Xgeva biosimilar EU launch about 3 months away, and five US ANDA approvals in the quarter; Denosumab US approval delayed by a few months.

rows.label: US CDMO breakeven
rows.why: Operating cost about INR60 crores per quarter, breakeven needs USD25-30 million annualised revenue, and CFO's 4-5 quarter view was contradicted by MD saying not within 12 months.

rows.label: Occlutech MedTech contribution
rows.why: Acquisition closed mid-July with FY27 sales target about INR400 crores over about 8.5 months and breakeven EBITDA; ex-diligence ortho/MedTech Q1 EBITDA loss about INR5-7 crores.

rows.label: Daman OAI resolution
rows.why: OAI status at Daman, which supplies about 45% of US revenue; CAPA initiated with resolution expected in 6-12 months, while management says supplies are uninterrupted.

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
539524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 154 crore in Q4 FY25
vs Rs 156 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Swasthfit (preventive B2C brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed 27% of FY26 total revenue; management says B2C is about 75% of revenue and packages make up about 28% of revenue, including Suburban packages.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Sustained double-digit growth through the year, with added testing locations to improve turnaround time.

segments.name: West / Suburban
segments.commentary: Suburban had weak performance for about 3 quarters but showed recovery in Q4; it is now reported within West and is no longer a separate entity.

segments.name: Radiology (Sovaaka and centres)
segments.commentary: One Sovaaka premium centre launched in January 2026; no further Sovaaka centres planned in FY27. One or two radiology centres are in the FY27 capex plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at early-to-mid-teens; CEO later framed it as a 13%-15% range.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 27%-28%, similar to FY26's 27.2% including the Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 100-120 crore, covering maintenance capex plus 12-15 new labs, radiology centres and a precision lab.
Effective tax rate expected to stay around 25%.
Price increase not planned immediately; a decision is a few quarters away, depending on market response and competition.
International expansion: a Dubai/UAE subsidiary incorporated; over 3-5 years, new geographies including the Middle East are planned on top of Nepal and Bangladesh.
capex_capacity: FY26: added 14 new labs and more than 1,100 collection centres; about 32 labs and close to 2,000 collection centres added over two years.
FY27 plan: 12-15 new labs, 1-2 radiology centres and a precision diagnostic lab, on top of maintenance capex within Rs 100-120 crore.
Acquired Shahbazkers Diagnostic Centre, a single pathology-led lab in Mumbai with about Rs 6 crore revenue, for about Rs 20 crore (about 3.3x FY26 revenue); the EBITDA margin was not disclosed.
Sovaaka: one centre launched January 2026; management wants to stabilise it before any expansion.
Radiology expansion is to be slow and calibrated, with no ambitious 4-5 year targets set.
demand_pricing: FY26 patient volume growth was 5.3% (vs 4.2% in FY25); Q4 patient volume growth was 8.2%; sample volume growth was 12.9% in Q4 and 10.4% in FY26.
Tests per patient rose to 3.21 in Q4 from 3.07; revenue per patient growth was attributed to test and geographic mix.
About 39% of revenue now comes from Tier 3-plus towns; management says pricing is set by cluster, so Tier 3 growth is not dilutive.
Price increase deferred: last price rise was 3 years ago, but management is waiting because it passed on GST-related benefits.
Management said GLP-1 drugs had no differential impact on volumes.
Reagent supply: about 3-4 months of inventory and long-term contracts; a prolonged Middle East conflict could affect imported reagent supply and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expense up sharply in Q4, and is the margin sustainable into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Suburban's revenue or margin separately reported, and where does its margin stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT declined 15% YoY to Rs 132 crore despite revenue growth, partly due to the absence of the Rs 41 crore one-time benefit from last year.
Margin pressure from heavy investment in labs, infrastructure and A&P; FY27 margin guided at 27-28%, which is flat to FY26.
Reagent and consumable supply and cost risk from the Middle East conflict after about 3-4 months of inventory.
Patient volume growth of 8.2% in Q4 may not be sustainable; management cautioned against building it into FY27 plans.
Price increase timing is uncertain; competitive intensity and market response will determine it.
Suburban recovery and West margin improvement are not separately disclosed, which limits tracking.

key_quotes: We are entering FY27 with strong operational momentum, a strengthened digital infrastructure, and a clear pathway towards sustaining early to mid -teens revenue growth.
So the 8.2% patient volume growth that we have seen in this quarter is something which I would not hastily built into the plan for next year.

539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: Swasthfit (bundled wellness packages)
segments.commentary: Growing about 20% YoY, but its share of revenue is flat at about 27% because total revenue grew at a similar pace. Management expects this growth to be sustained.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.
Capex of about Rs 140-150 crore per year; 12-15 lab additions planned for FY27 and 3-4 radiology centres (Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns).
International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.
Plans to add 12-15 labs in FY27, similar to last year; network addition numbers are disclosed once a year.
Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.
Capacity utilisation is not disclosed; management says capacity is never a constraint in pathology.
Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 8.2% was spread across geographies; management said it is too early to call a sustained shift from the 5.5-6% levels of two quarters ago, because the fever season has not yet started.
CGHS/ECHS price revision is worth about 2-3% of realisations; the rest of the 10% rise in revenue per patient came from test and geography mix, per management.
Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.
Gross margin is near 81%. Management says higher-realisation tests carry higher COGS, so margin is unlikely to improve significantly.
Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation growth comes from CGHS/ECHS, and will it continue for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guidance be upgraded from 27-28% margin and mid-teens growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is more likely to be mid-teens than early teens; margin guidance will be reviewed after Q2, with a lean towards reinvestment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Neuome (30% stake, up to Rs 3.5 crore) is a diagnostic supply-chain innovation play with operational benefit, not a new business. International is a long-term project: Ghana (80% of Sunshine Healthcare, up to GHS 45.6 million) and a Dubai subsidiary, with focus on Africa, Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia; no target set.

qa_highlights.question: How should the cash of about Rs 1,700 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily M&A to build presence in the West and South, plus high-end radiology centres as capex on top of maintenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.

risks_watch: Margin guidance of 27-28% is not revised until after Q2; the CGHS/ECHS price pass-through is expected to support margins for only one or two more quarters, so the margin trajectory in H2 depends on reinvestment choices.

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)

segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.

FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Mobavenue Neural Engine launched as a unified AI layer at the core of GMP360; management said core decisioning moved fully to neural network systems in FY26.

Data and supply costs are the largest cost line and are largely variable with revenue.
Named global competitors: AppLovin, Unity and The Trade Desk; named India competitors: Affle and InMobi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.

539682|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR 767 million, with EBITDA margin steady at 21.1% and PAT up 54.8% to INR 113 million.
539682|2026-09.overview: Mobavenue reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 767 million, up 41.3% YoY and 5.4% QoQ, with H1 revenue of INR 1,496 million up 48.6%. Gross margin widened to 41.5% as supply-end data cost fell to 58.5% of revenue from 61.5% a year ago. EBITDA was INR 660 million at a 21.1% margin, and PAT was INR 113 million at a 14.7% margin. Employee costs rose 62.3% YoY as the company invested ahead of growth, while international revenue share doubled to 23.8%.

qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth of about 49% at 21% EBITDA exceeds the 30% framework; RPO up about 10% to INR 50.67 and international share at 23.8% support confidence. No numeric target was set.

qa_highlights.question: What drove EBITDA margin above 20% for three consecutive quarters and what is the medium-term outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an outcome-based revenue model, an asset-light cost structure and operating leverage as revenue grows faster than costs. It reiterated the rule-of-50 framework.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international vs India RPO difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give ranges; it said emerging markets have slightly higher RPO than India and the US and UK are higher still, and that the blended figure is used in modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Is PiiX generating revenue and how is it performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue contribution was not quantified; PiiX was launched about 5 months ago and is being used as a utility to speed advertiser onboarding. Management expects revenue to build over time, with advertiser adds as the year-end metric.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the direct-client share decline, and what is the channel mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a relative decline, citing agency and reseller routes for entry into emerging markets. It is hiring direct teams and expects the direct share to rise over the medium to long term.

qa_highlights.question: Can Mobavenue serve ads on chatbots and LLM platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Current chatbot ad systems are closed and search-intent driven. Mobavenue is integrating them and expects to access them as they open up to programmatic exchanges.

539686|2026-03.headline: K.P. Energy FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore (up 57% YoY) and Q4 PAT hit a record INR 78.69 crore.
539686|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR 1,505.54 crore (up 57% YoY), EBITDA of INR 328.44 crore (up 68%) and PAT of INR 181.4 crore (up 57%). Q4 net sales reached an all-time quarterly high of INR 631.81 crore, up 83% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 21% (up 194 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 78.69 crore. The order book is about 2 GW (INR 3,000 plus crore), with about 230 MW added in Q4, while operating cash flow weakened due to higher inventory (WTG turbines) and advances. Management guided to 40-50% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shabana Belim attributed it to a rise in inventory (WTG turbines) ahead of upcoming projects, amid geopolitical supply risk; debtors were broadly stable relative to revenue growth. Cash conversion cycle ranges from 100 to 150 days depending on customer.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital normalise once the geopolitical situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital will stay higher in proportion to 55% revenue growth plus upcoming order mobilisation; higher inventory will convert into debtors over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were in line with prior periods and EBITDA margin improved to 21.82% in FY26 from 20.46% in FY25; turbine-inclusive EPC contracts carry a somewhat lower margin than EPC-only contracts because of pre-booked turbine leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IPP unit generation and revenue decline in Q4 YoY?

539725|2026-09.headline: Gokul Agro Q2 FY27 revenue up 13% to INR7,481 crore; EBITDA up 41% to INR276 crore with margin at 3.68%.
539725|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 13% YoY to INR7,481 crore, with EBITDA including other income up 41% to INR276 crore and margin up about 74 bps to 3.68%. PAT rose 40% to INR150 crore, and H1 PAT grew 54% to INR274 crore on 10% revenue growth. Management attributed the growth mainly to better price realisations, with no volume growth expected this year as capacity is fully utilised. A 24 September 2026 change in edible oil import duties deferred trade purchases in September, lifting closing inventory, which management called a timing effect. This was the company's first earnings call, held to start a regular investor engagement.

segments.name: Edible oils

segments.commentary: Castor oil plus 12-HSA, hydrogenated castor oil and ricinoleic acid; no separate financials disclosed.

segments.name: Specialty fats
segments.commentary: Richfield, Pride, Biscopride, Chocosil and Rich Chef; described as a smaller share of volumes, with no figures given.

segments.name: Channel mix (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: B2B 79%, exports 13% (33 countries), B2C 8% of channel revenue, up from about 5-6% in FY26.

EBITDA margin expected to stay in a 3.5% to 4% range, with absolute EBITDA growing accordingly.

B2C marketing spend earmarked at under INR25 crore, to be spent gradually; B2C margins expected to be broadly in line with consolidated, with no large near-term expansion.
Next earnings calls to follow half-year and full-year results.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity: Gandhidham about 3,400 TPD refining, 3,200 TPD seed crushing and 300 TPD biodiesel; Krishnapatnam about 1,400 TPD refining; Haldia about 1,350 TPD refining; Mangalore facility (capacity not stated).
Capacity expansion of about 8 lakh tonnes per annum across the four manufacturing locations, with full operation expected by October 2027.
15 MW captive solar plant commissioned in Gujarat in Q1 FY27; further 4 MW Andhra Pradesh, 4 MW Karnataka and 10 MW Gujarat planned.
Oil palm: about 550 hectares completed in FY25-26, with 900 hectares under development for completion in FY27; current output about 1,000 tonnes per annum, under 1% of requirement.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the 13% Q2 revenue growth mainly to better price realisations; commodity prices rose 15% to 20%, and realisations track market prices.
Edible oil import duties revised effective 24 September 2026; trade deferred purchases in September, raising closing inventory. Management views this as temporary, with channel activity normalising.
Hedging: inventory largely sold through back-to-back physical forwards or hedged on CBOT and Malaysian exchanges; import payments hedged via forwards; open inventory held at 10% to 15%.

About 80% of raw material is imported. Stock-in-trade purchases rose to INR2,000 crore in Q2 from INR491 crore in Q1; management said trading sales are usually 10% to 20% of volume and under 15% in H1.
Distribution spans more than 650 dealers and distributors across 28 states and UTs, with a new Jammu and Kashmir depot and Vitalife push in Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Karnataka.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth was driven mainly by better price realisations. Volume growth is not expected this year because capacity is fully utilised; new capex is underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is the roughly 3.5% margin sustainable, or does it include inventory or forex gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, citing branding, value-added mix, better utilisation, smarter sourcing and cost control, with no mention of inventory or forex gains.

qa_highlights.question: How is the business insulated from edible oil price and forex volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is back-to-back sold or hedged, import payments are forward-hedged, and open inventory is held at 10% to 15%. No derivatives are used for forex.

qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 10% next year and 10% to 15% annually after that, with EBITDA margin at 3.5% to 4%; capacity arrives by October 2027.

qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise realisations and EBITDA per tonne were not disclosed. B2C margins are roughly in line with consolidated 3.5%, with marketing spend under INR25 crore and FY26 spend not disclosed.

539872|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.3% YoY to INR165.6 crore with gross margin up 210 bps to 48.3%; management guides 10-15% revenue growth for FY27.
539872|2026-06.overview: Bajaj Healthcare reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR165.6 crore, up 11.3% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR29.6 crore (17.8% margin) and PAT from continuing operations of INR13.9 crore (8.4% margin). Domestic API was the main growth driver at INR92.3 crore (up 27% YoY), while exports (INR50.1 crore) and formulations (INR23.3 crore) contributed the rest. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% and EBITDA margins of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28, and reiterated pipeline timelines for peptide, oncology API, and CDMO/novel-drug launches. Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end, and the call was the company's first earnings call.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR92.3 crore, up 27% YoY; management said API prices were broadly stable QoQ and the growth was not price-led. Ascorbic acid and salts contribute about 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.1 crore in Q1. Magnesium L-Threonate (nutraceutical ingredient supplied to a US innovator) is the largest export product at about 10% of FY26 revenue, with FY27 growth guided at 15-20%. Management expects export share to rise to 30-35% over time.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.3 crore in Q1. Cenobamate CDMO launch expected to add INR10-12 crore in FY27; Oncocare brand business covers 15+ brands across 23 states and 3 UTs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% YoY; profit growth guided at a similar rate. FY28 top-line growth also guided at a similar rate.
EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28.
Capex of INR40-50 crore every year over the next few years.
Medium term: management said INR900-1,000 crore revenue achievable in the next two to three years.
Revenue mix expected to normalise as exports improve and geopolitical conditions ease over the year.
Receivable days expected to settle at 110-120 days going forward.
capex_capacity: Peptide plant: installed capacity about 250 kg per annum, commissioning targeted for Q4 2027. Management said peak revenue at full utilisation could be INR200-300 crore at 18-20% EBITDA margin, ramping over two to three years.
Oncology API dedicated facility: commercial target Q4 2028.
Gen Rx Pharmaceutical facility in Nashik (solid dosage forms): acquisition pending NCLT approval; commercial production expected in H2 2027.
Savli DSIR-approved R&D centre expansion of over 10,000 sq ft, expected to be operational by August 2026, housing 100+ researchers. R&D spend rose from 0.4% of sales in 2024 to 2.2% in 2026.
Three loss-making Tarapur plants: one sold, two remain with no buyer yet; sale proceeds not quantified.
demand_pricing: API prices stable QoQ in Q1; management said future pricing depends on geopolitical developments and oil prices.
Semaglutide (first peptide planned) market price cited at USD120-150 per gram. Plant is designed for global markets, with initial work for India.
CDMO: DMFs filed in UK and EU and six CEP approvals received in the last 6-8 months. Management said first customer revenue could come at end-FY28, with quantum not yet estimated.
Cenobamate: SEC recommendation received; DCGI NOC and state licence still pending; tie-ups with eight Indian marketing companies, with the company acting as CDMO partner.
Suvorexant: BE studies completed; commercialisation expected Q4 FY28 because the patent is still in force.

Vitamin C is about 8-9% of revenue; backward integration via ICT MoU expected to complete in 2029. Eight to ten API molecules being backward-integrated, expected to be 20-25% of revenue, with a 1-2% margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: Was domestic API growth driven by volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said API prices were stable QoQ, implying the growth was volume-led; it added that the outlook depends on geopolitics and oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and profit growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 10-15% for FY27, with profit growth expected at a similar rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial timeline for the peptide plant and the expected revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant commissioning Q4 2027 with Semaglutide as the first product. Peak revenue of INR200-300 crore at full utilisation, with 18-20% EBITDA margin. Management said commercial revenue would begin in 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable days trend and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end; management expects 110-120 days going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and acquisition outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR40-50 crore each year. No further acquisitions planned until Gen Rx is commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: What working capital and inventory drivers apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory rose in Q4 FY26 on war-related precautionary buying; the longer-term increase reflects a shift from a few high-volume products pre-COVID to a larger product basket.

risks_watch: Commercial launch timelines for peptide (Q4 2027), oncology API (Q4 2028), Gen Rx (H2 2027) and CDMO (end-FY28) all depend on approvals or commissioning and have not been demonstrated yet.
Cenobamate revenue of INR10-12 crore in FY27 depends on pending DCGI NOC and state licence.
Receivables are high at 131 days; the 110-120 day target depends on customer behaviour, including government and institutional clients.
Inventory has risen sharply versus FY21 on a broader product mix.
Two Tarapur loss-making plants remain unsold.
Opioid-derivative intermediates are still in R&D, and the Government of India discussion on capacity is unresolved.
Management declined to name most peptide molecules, citing confidentiality.

539872|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores and PAT 26.9% to INR14.1 crores, with formulations up 82%.

EBITDA rose 12.2% YoY to INR32.1 crores at an 18.2% margin, while gross margin fell to 48.3% amid West Asia disruption. Formulations (INR41.7 crores, up 82% YoY) and export API (INR62.6 crores, up 28.5%) offset a weaker domestic API line (INR71.6 crores, down from INR76.3 crores). Management reiterated FY29 targets of INR900-1,000 crores revenue and 18-21% EBITDA margin, and flagged higher inventory held as a precaution against Gulf disruption.

Genrx acquisition to handle non-Baroda formulation volumes; new molecules to be made at Baroda, which is an approved facility.
demand_pricing: Cenobamate API tablets approved by DCGI (first in India, six strengths), launched commercially in September 2026; repeat orders received from partners, but secondary sales not yet known.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital inventory rise and will it normalise by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the higher inventory is a deliberate policy decision to avoid stoppages from the Gulf dispute; management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.answer: Genrx: INR200-250 crores in two to three years after start-up. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after it is in operation.

qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected above INR30 crores for FY27; Q2 operating cash flow about INR15 crores; receivable days improved from 145 to 135.

539876|2026-09.headline: Crompton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA 24.1% to Rs 205 Cr, with margin up 40 bps to 9%.
539876|2026-09.overview: Crompton delivered its third straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, with all business segments growing double digits per management. PBT excluding exceptional items grew 36.2%; the prior-year quarter carried a Rs 20 Cr Baroda plant restructuring exceptional, which inflates reported PAT growth of 65%. Management said price increases of about 80% of cost inflation have been passed through, supply disruptions from Q1 are over, and inventory days are back to year-ago levels. E-commerce was subdued due to a channel repositioning, and A&P spend was lower in H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 employee cost jump and the sustainable run rate?

Management said about INR7.5-8 crores are exceptional, leaving a regular quarterly run rate of about INR45-46 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core volume growth fall so sharply in Q4 and is there market share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Q4 branded volume fell about 5% and core about 3%, due to a low export base; it denied share loss and reiterated double-digit core volume growth as the aspiration.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin gains flow through to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sequential gross margin rose from about 26% when milk was INR40 to 28% at INR42, and expects to reach double-digit EBITDA over coming years, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the INR730 crore inventory increase?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crores of the increase is rate variance from inflation; quantity variance is nil, and powder inventory is expected to fall as that business shrinks.

539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
539889|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)
segments.commentary: 61% of Q1 revenue; volume down 2% YoY on transient slowdown in certain channels, value up 10%. B2C grew strongly while B2B declined modestly; B2C flagship growth was 'high single digit to close to double digit'. Dahi now included in flagship (previously in Others).

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth above 10%, with Q2 and Q3 supported by festive demand.
Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.
Management aspires to return flagship B2C growth to double digits; B2B will be pursued where margins allow.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over about 1.5 years, targeted by March 2028.
Doubling cheese capacity to be paired with a parallel expansion in whey protein generation; milk procurement to be scaled up to match.
Renewable energy: a solar JV with Tata Power Solar; biogas power from farm (about 5,000 cattle); the investment value was INR4.6 crores per the annual report, not INR50 crores.
demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.
Management said Google searches and website traffic rose about 200% over the last two months, after the India's Got Latent association.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume also grew strongly and that prices rose in stages, not 100%; new products and lower-cost protein entry formats contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said milk cost pass-through was complete in Q1 at INR42/litre, and the mix gain was offset by milk inflation; gross profit growth matched revenue growth at 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are core-category volumes falling despite wider distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is in B2B, where volumes were given up to protect profitability; B2C is not declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can B2B channel losses be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers or channels or give numbers, citing commercial sensitivity; B2B deals are short-term and come and go.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost, timeline or ROI, calling it a special commercial deal aimed at awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income spike in alternate quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income is usually higher in March due to annual fair-value gains on biological assets (cattle); Q1 FY26 also had a one-off gain on sale of the idle Sonipat plant.

risks_watch: Flagship volume decline (-2%) and B2B channel losses; watch whether B2C growth reaches double digits and offsets B2B.

Milk price stability versus monsoon and festive demand pressure, and dependence on price hikes for pass-through.

539889|2026-09.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,241 crore, up 23% YoY, with volumes up 12% and EBITDA up 37% excluding last year's one-off.
539889|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR1,241 crore, with about half the growth from volume (12%) and the rest from price and mix. Gross profit rose 24% to INR323 crore and gross margin was 26% versus 25.8% a year ago, with gross margin per litre up from INR14 to INR17 despite milk costs rising about INR7 per litre. EBITDA excluding last year's FX MTM one-off was INR101 crore (8.1% margin, up 37%), and PAT grew 42% to INR42 crore. Net debt rose to INR678 crore from INR484 crore in March 2026, driven by inventory build-up from inflation and festive stocking, and management expects debt to stay in a similar range.

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, curd)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR778 crore in Q2, up 20% in value and 7% in volume. Paneer had its strongest volume quarter; ghee grew double digits in volume; Gowardhan holds 22% share in branded cow ghee.

segments.name: New Age (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR154 crore, up 71% YoY and 12% of revenue. Avvatar reports about 15% online whey protein share and over 75% of its revenue from quick commerce, e-commerce and its own website.

segments.name: Ingredients (MPC, lactose)
segments.commentary: Management said this segment grew exceptionally well in Q2, led by milk protein concentrate and lactose. No figures were given.

segments.name: Regions
segments.commentary: All four regions grew at high double digits; South and West were the fastest-growing. Regional disclosure was added this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects high single-digit volume growth in core categories (paneer, ghee) in coming quarters, with no price increase planned in core categories.
Milk prices are not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought and deficient rains; procurement is at about INR46.5/litre and may hold through Q3.
Blended gross margin of 26-27% is expected to continue, with no dilution from new capacity.
A&P spend is expected to stay in the INR130-150 crore annual range; ~INR20 crore of Q2 spend is treated as non-recurring.
Net debt is not expected to fall materially; it may rise marginally as capex is funded. Management expects positive operating cash flow for FY27 as inventory unwinds.
New Age business targets a ~25% revenue share on the way to the INR10,000 crore ambition; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 growth numbers.
capex_capacity: Paneer: capacity rising 4x from 20 to 80 metric tons per day across Manchar and Palamaner, about INR100 crore, commissioning by June 2027; management expects about 80% utilisation soon after commissioning.

Cheese: capacity doubling from 60 to 120 metric tons per day for about INR105 crore at existing sites, phased 80, 100, then 120, with completion targeted for Q2 FY28; whey protein output doubles with it.
Combined capex of INR205 crore approved; management separately described a capex outlay of over INR200 crore for the year.
Board approved amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms into the company, subject to approvals.
Capex has been funded from internal accruals over the past three years; ECLGS 5.0 working capital funding and a new consortium lender were added this year.
demand_pricing: Two price increases were taken in the quarter; no further core-category price increase is planned.
Organised paneer share is low: management estimates 70-80% of out-of-home paneer is analogue, and about 4 million kg/day of paneer is consumed in India.
B2C grew double digits in Q2 and B2B was deliberately limited, as in Q1; overall mix is about 70% B2C and 30% B2B.
Management sees no price war from Milky Mist's capacity expansion (100 to 350 for paneer/cheese); it cites brand strength and distribution as its edge.
Management said blended gross margin is 26-27% and that cheese and whey are assessed together; no product-level margins are disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 7% flagship volume growth came from B2C festive stocking versus institutional buying, and how much of the INR177 crore other expenses is non-recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C grew double digits in both Q2 and last year's Q2, and B2B was consciously limited. About INR20 crore of Q2 spend is one-off brand building; the rest is variable cost (power, fuel, supply chain) and A&P within an annual budget.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view New Age growth and margins going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: New Age revenue reached INR154 crore in Q2 (INR118 crore in Q1, INR100 crore in Q4 FY26), an ARR above INR600 crore. Management did not give FY28 growth numbers but targets about 25% New Age share at the INR10,000 crore milestone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for milk procurement cost in Q3 and Q4, given South cooperative price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Milk is at INR46.5/litre and is not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought. Karnataka's KMF raised prices, and some South response is possible; the South is 20-25% of procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory and net debt high, and will cash flow turn positive by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the rise mainly to inflation and festive inventory; inventory days are stable. It expects the inventory build to unwind by year-end and believes FY27 operating cash flow will be positive.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement, and how will the new cheese and whey capacity affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin per litre rose from INR14 to INR17 despite milk up INR7/litre; ingredients (MPC, lactose) grew strongly. Management says blended margin of 26-27% will hold as cheese and whey capacity doubles.

qa_highlights.question: What is the paneer and cheese capacity ramp, and what utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Paneer reaches 80 MT/day by June 2027 and could be about 80% utilised right away (roughly INR500-600 crore incremental revenue was suggested by an analyst). Cheese phases from 60 to 80 MT next month or so, then 100 and 120 MT by Q2 FY28; management assumes 80% utilisation.

risks_watch: Working capital and net debt (INR678 crore) are elevated; the company says FY27 operating cash flow should turn positive as inventory unwinds, which needs to be tracked.

Capacity additions (paneer June 2027, cheese Q2 FY28) depend on demand absorption; new competitors such as Milky Mist are expanding paneer and cheese capacity.
Gross margin guidance of 26-27% is blended, and the company does not disclose product-level margins, which limits visibility into New Age and cheese economics.

So I don't see any price war and all this things. It's only the ability to sell the brand, which we have and the distribution is very important.

539957|2026-03.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.
539957|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 average sales volume rose 6.15% YoY to 4.672 mmscmd, with CNG at 3.349 mmscmd and DPNG at 0.605 mmscmd. FY26 EBITDA fell to INR1,451 crore from INR1,570 crore and PAT to INR847 crore from INR1,041 crore. Management declined to give firm FY27 margin guidance, saying it would prioritise volume growth and pass through costs only where alternate-fuel pricing allows.

540005|2026-03.headline: LTM Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ to USD 1.22bn (8.1% YoY) while Q4 operating EBIT margin fell 100bps QoQ to 15.1% on partial wage hikes.
540005|2026-03.overview: LTM closed FY2026 with revenue of USD 4.76bn (6% USD growth, 5.3% constant currency) and operating EBIT margin of 15.4%, up 90bps. Q4 revenue grew 1.2% QoQ and 8.1% YoY in USD, with order inflow steady at USD 1.7bn, the sixth straight quarter above USD 1.5bn. Q4 margin dipped to 15.1% from 16.1% in Q3 due to a partial wage hike effective 1 January, partly offset by forex. Management introduced the Lakshya'31 five-year strategy (goal to double revenue in five years), a move to four reporting segments from Q1 FY27, and declined to give numeric FY27 guidance.

540005|2026-09.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.
540005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was USD 1.235bn, up 1.1% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, with INR revenue of Rs 11,808 crores (+13.6% YoY). EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?

540025|2026-03.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 2,034 million, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin steady at 31%.
540025|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR 2,034 million (+22% YoY, +18% QoQ) and FY26 revenue reached INR 7,458 million (+17%), both record levels per management. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to INR 632 million at a 31% margin, and PAT rose 69% YoY to INR 453 million (22% margin). Human Healthcare, Animal Healthcare, Bioprocessing and Specialized Manufacturing all grew on a YoY basis, with Serratiopeptidase volumes a key driver. Management flagged input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) and a challenging US market, and guided to steady margins and a double-digit growth aspiration for FY27 without quantified guidance.

rows.why: Subsidiary fermentation can add a 50% capacity increment with infrastructure already in place, with the decision after September 2026; Nashik R&D centre (threefold research capacity in phase 1) expected operational in H2 FY27, but the main-company capacity call is deferred past September.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Growth is volume-driven: Serratiopeptidase YTD about +45%, Q4 Human Healthcare +24% YoY, FY26 revenue +17%, and management aspires to double-digit FY27 growth, though US is only expected to grow 'little'.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not quantified and main-company expansion decision is explicitly deferred to after September; R&D capex of about INR 50 crore in FY27 (INR 130 crore total) is already planned, so a main-company capex announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given; management frames FY27 as 'very challenging' with steady margins and only a double-digit aspiration, and US revenue fell about 11% YoY in INR in Q4 per analyst calculation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) is absorbed at about 10% of tariff cost with pass-through only from FY27, and US margin impact could be 1-2%, so margin pressure is possible before price increases land.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Anti-inflammatory enzyme EU novel food approval is expected this year (top product was 23% of FY26 revenue), which could give 5-10 years of exclusivity, but no numbers were given and approval timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Price increases to pass on cost inflation from FY27
rows.why: Management plans price increases from the new year to offset inflation, but Indian Serratiopeptidase pricing is broadly constant today and tariffs are only about 10% absorbed-and-passed gradually.

rows.label: Biocatalysis moderate growth in FY27
rows.why: FY26 biocatalysis revenue was INR 247 million vs INR 174 million in FY25 (+42%), with management guiding only 'moderate' FY27 growth and facing regulatory and competitive challenges.

rows.label: Buyback or capital return from INR 700 crore cash
rows.why: Chairman said the board will evaluate options including buyback against INR 700 crore cash and no interim dividend, but no decision has been announced.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record and long-term positioning but cautious on the US outlook, cost pass-through and product-level detail, and called FY27 'very challenging'; analysts pushed on gross margin moderation, US strategy, pricing vs volume and capital allocation.

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.

segments.name: Human Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,139 million, down 7% YoY and 11% QoQ on lower Pharma API sales; 60% of revenue. India sales INR 580 million (vs INR 659 million YoY, INR 699 million QoQ); international INR 559 million (vs INR 552 million YoY, INR 582 million QoQ). B2C USD 1.14 million vs USD 1.12 million a year ago.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 252 million, down 3% YoY and up 1% QoQ; 13% of revenue.

segments.name: Bioprocessing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 306 million, up 30% YoY and down 5% QoQ, driven by Food business; 16% of revenue.

segments.name: Specialized Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 200 million, up 41% YoY and 11% QoQ; 11% of revenue.

segments.name: Biocatalysis (within reporting)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 45 million vs INR 44 million in Q4 FY26; management expects stronger growth in H2 FY27.

segments.name: JC Biotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 195 million (vs INR 211 million YoY), EBITDA INR 26 million (vs INR 33 million), PAT INR 10 million (vs INR 14 million).

segments.name: evoxx (subsidiary, Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 million (vs INR 70 million YoY), EBITDA negative INR 13 million, PAT negative INR 18 million (vs EBITDA INR 14 million and PAT INR 7 million a year ago).

segments.name: SciTech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 201 million (vs INR 145 million YoY), EBITDA INR 31 million, PAT INR 13 million (vs negative PAT INR 8 million a year ago).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 86 million in Q1 FY26 (4.62% of revenue)

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 120-130 crore capex to be spent in FY27 and what is the growth component?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed INR 123 crore for FY27, about INR 20 crore may slip to Q2; about INR 20 crore maintenance, INR 50 crore R&D facility, balance growth. Fermentation utilisation is around 70-75%, with a capacity decision next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US growth lagging the market, and what is the reason for the about 14% decline in international Human Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a weak US environment, the shift to branding most ingredients (which takes time), geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges; expects US growth of 8-10% at most at this juncture.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 growth reach 12%+ given the sales reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects double-digit growth in the balance three quarters; the INR 10 crore incremental reversal (about 8% drag) is expected to come back in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sales reversal normalise, and what caused it?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were booked but still in transit at quarter end, so revenue was not recognised; the incremental reversal was INR 100 million over normal quarterly reversals and has already been recorded as of the call date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% EBITDA margin achievable, and will energy costs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to return to about 30% and cited 30-32% as the target, with energy costs easing from Q2 through operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of novel food approval and the EFSA process?
qa_highlights.answer: Still under EFSA consideration; management said it could take three to six months, depending on authorities, and the process is on and off.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products and markets are driving future growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track product-level sales; 15-20 molecules are in the pipeline, with expansion into biocatalysis, animal feed, ruminant, food, baking and detergent; bioenergy has no revenue yet and is deferred to after the new R&D facility next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position at June 30, 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory about INR 190 crore, receivables about INR 131 crore, payables about INR 41 crore, net working capital about INR 280 crore; working capital cycle about 125-138 days.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margin to return to about 30% for the full year, with 30-32% EBITDA margin cited as the target range for the rest of FY27.
Double-digit revenue growth expected for the balance three quarters of FY27; management says the Q1 INR 100 million incremental sales reversal (about 8% growth drag) should reverse in Q2.
Margin recovery expected from lower power and fuel costs and operational efficiency from Q2 onward.
US business guided to about 8-10% growth at current juncture; management said about 8% by year-end, and US is not expected to exceed 8-10% near term.
Biocatalysis expected to deliver good growth in H2 FY27.

International Human Nutrition declined about 14% in the quarter; management attributed this to US business shift toward branding of ingredients, geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges.

Top 10 customers about 23% of revenue (27% a year ago); top 10 products about 45% (49% in Q4 FY26). Management said 70-80% of customers are constant and 20-30% of business changes each period.
Specialized Manufacturing up 41% YoY; Bioprocessing up 30% YoY on Food business; Animal Healthcare down 3% YoY.
Europe (evoxx) revenue INR 74 million, growth mainly from food area per management. SciTech revenue INR 201 million vs INR 145 million a year ago.

Protein hydrolysis products began generating sales in the quarter; sugar-management patent (Alternansucrase) granted in the US.

Revenue timing: INR 100 million extra export reversal shows dependence on shipment timing; Q2 must show reversal and double-digit growth.
Product concentration: serratiopeptidase dependence is high; regulatory/ban news flagged, though management says impact is about 1%.
Pricing and competition on the largest product: management declined to quantify realisation changes.

Governance/disclosure: management declined to disclose serratiopeptidase numbers, Starya Labs is not yet operational, and inventory and several questions were deferred.
key_quotes: Our fundamentals remain strong, execution continues to be solid, and we are well positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities.

540025|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious and defensive: management described Q1 as soft and muted, blamed geopolitics, energy costs and US business changes, and repeatedly deflected QoQ and product-level questions while keeping FY27 guidance of double-digit growth and about 30% margin.

540025|2026-09.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR2,145 million and EBITDA margin reached 34%, with management guiding 30-32% margins going forward.
540025|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR2,145 million, up 16% YoY and 12% QoQ, while H1 revenue grew 10% to INR4,062 million. EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR721 million (34% margin vs 33% a year ago and 28% in Q1), and PAT rose 14% YoY to INR512 million (24% margin). Management said deferred sales of about INR10 crore from Q1 were only partly recovered (INR2.5 crore net), with INR7.5 crore carried into the next quarter. Management urged investors to assess the business on an annual basis rather than quarterly.

segments.name: Human Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,285 million, +6% YoY and +11% QoQ, driven by Pharma/API, Biocatalysis and Nutrition; flat on YTD basis. Biocatalysis within Human Healthcare was INR66 million in Q2 vs about INR45 million in Q1.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR265 million, +37% YoY, +5% QoQ and +14% YTD; about 12% of group revenue.

segments.name: Bio-Processing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR365 million, +43% YoY, +19% QoQ and +37% in H1; about 17% of group revenue.

segments.name: Specialized Manufacturing (SciTech)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR231 million (segment reported), +25% YoY, +15% QoQ, +32% in H1; subsidiary SciTech reported Q2 revenue INR234 million, EBITDA INR61 million and PAT INR36 million, with H1 EBITDA up 144% and PAT about 6x YoY.

segments.name: JC Biotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR200 million (vs INR186 million), EBITDA INR29 million (vs INR37 million), PAT INR17 million (flat); H1 revenue INR395 million vs INR397 million.

segments.name: Evoxx (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR75 million, EBITDA INR4 million, loss of INR7 million (vs loss of INR18 million in Q1 and PAT of INR14 million a year ago); H1 loss INR26 million vs INR21 million profit last year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guided at 30-32% on an overall basis for calculation purposes.
Management expects progressive momentum through the year and expects the U.S. market to pick up toward year-end, with a possible margin upside if it does.
Long-run growth intent is double digits, mid to lower-mid double digits; FY27 segment guidance to come after February-March budgeting.
Capex guidance for FY27 unchanged at about INR123 crore (including R&D and maintenance); about INR52 crore already spent in H1.
Human Healthcare Pharma/API expected to recover further toward year-end.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance of about INR123 crore including R&D and maintenance; about INR52 crore spent in H1.
SciTech capacity utilisation rose with added shifts, improving efficiencies; the company did not give specific capacity figures.
R&D spend INR90 million in Q2 (vs INR86 million) and INR216 million in H1 (vs INR166 million); about 4.3% of consolidated revenue after intercompany elimination vs 3% in Q2 FY26.
demand_pricing: U.S. market described as dull for the first two quarters due to global conditions; management expects pick-up toward year-end, citing SupplySide West interest and new potential customers, with timing of one to two quarters.

Growth is coming from food, animal feed and Biocatalysis; management said it is adding new customers and geographies rather than relying on existing clients, and existing clients in the U.S. are not growing rapidly.
Top-10 customers were 26% of Q2 revenue (vs 27%) and 22% in H1 (vs 23%). B2C revenue was USD 0.91 million in H1 (vs USD 1.29 million).
New products and applications contributed about 7-8% of revenue, per management's approximate estimate.
Management said Novonesis's large capex in India is aimed at bioethanol, where Advanced Enzyme is not present; current revenue is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: Would underlying sales growth be 12-13% or 10-11% after adjusting for Q1 deferment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR10 crore was deferred in Q1, of which INR2.5 crore was recovered net and INR7.5 crore carried into next quarter; the target is lower double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving SciTech's margin and revenue scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is broad-based, driven by added shifts, higher capacity utilisation, efficiency gains, a wider customer base and R&D projects now paying off.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost fell from INR45 crore in Q1 to INR40 crore in Q2; what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Drop attributed to a about INR1 crore provision reversal, ESOP cost reversal for departed employees, and lower U.S. headcount; management declined to fix a sustainable run rate as hiring continues.

qa_highlights.question: What is cash balance after the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was about INR640 crore at 30 September and about INR610 crore after roughly INR30 crore spent in October, excluding October accruals. Buyback: 2.41 million shares at average INR289.09.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Biocatalysis business trending and what is its size?
qa_highlights.answer: Biocatalysis within Human Healthcare was INR66 million in Q2 vs about INR45 million in Q1; management expects most Human Healthcare growth to come from it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of WELLFA, the B2C brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is negligible; it has been separated into its own company, and management is not counting on material revenue for the next two to three years. It declined to give a 3-year revenue target of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: U.S. recovery timing: management has pointed to one to two quarters, but the U.S. has underperformed for several quarters.
Q1 deferred sales (about INR7.5 crore carried forward) must be recognised in Q3 to sustain growth.
Employee cost run rate uncertain after one-off reversals in Q2; hiring is ongoing.
Evoxx remains loss-making (H1 loss INR26 million).
Input costs for power, fuel and raw materials remained elevated, per management.
Dependence on the company's largest product, where competitor supply disruptions have helped; management declined to share product revenue.
