540047|2026-03.headline: Dilip Buildcon FY26 consolidated PAT rose to INR1,398 crores on revenue down 20.6% to INR8,984 crores; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores.
540047|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue fell about 22% to INR7,005 crores, while standalone EBITDA dropped about 19% to INR734 crores and standalone PAT rose to INR841 crores from INR311 crores. Consolidated EBITDA was INR1,766 crores at a 19.6% margin. Management reframed the company into three verticals (EPC, MDO coal mining, and Assets/InvIT) and targets 75% of profit from long-term assets by FY29. Management guided FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40%, EBITDA margin of 11-12%, and INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders, with net debt-free status targeted by FY28.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Builds assets for the group; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores and completions INR2,812 crores. Management targets INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders in FY27 and 30-40% revenue growth.

segments.name: MDO (coal mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 coal production 28.72 million tonnes (Siarmal 22.35 Mt, Pachhwara 6.37 Mt). Revenue from mining about INR1,600 crores currently, guided to about INR2,500 crores in FY27, about INR3,100 crores in FY28 and about INR4,000 crores in FY29. Target 57 Mt by FY29.

segments.name: Assets / InvIT
segments.commentary: Holds about INR1,600 crores of InvIT units. Next tranche of 11 HAM assets expected to yield about INR1,800 crores of InvIT units for incremental investment of INR169 crores, with transfers through Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40% over FY26, supported by an order book of almost INR28,000 crores.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin target of 11-12%.
Targeting INR10,000-12,000 crores of new order inflow in FY27.
Standalone debt reduction of INR600-800 crores in FY27; interest outgo expected at INR375-400 crores; net debt-free by FY28.
Coal production target of about 57 Mt by FY29; Siarmal about 33-35 Mt in FY27 and 50 Mt by FY29.
Management expects about 75% of profit from long-term assets and 25% from EPC by FY29.

Transmission and solar projects: equity requirement about INR1,600 crores (solar about INR1,200 crores, transmission about INR400 crores); DBL targets 15% of equity with 85% from outside investors; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR in high teens; commissioning about 2 years from start.
capex_capacity: Siarmal coal handling plant capex pending; a revenue-share kicker applies once it reaches COD.
Pottangi mine to be set up over the next 3 years.
Next InvIT tranche: 11 HAM assets, transfers 4 assets in Q1 FY27 and the balance in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
Under-construction projects of about INR1,000 crores plus invested, to be transferred to InvIT.
Gross block about INR3,600 crores and net block about INR800 crores, stated to be debt free.
demand_pricing: Average monthly infrastructure tendering in FY26 was about INR1.4 trillion, below the government's FY26 target, due to state elections, regulatory scrutiny and administrative delays.

Bitumen and HSD (diesel) cost inflation from elevated crude prices; government contracts only partly pass this through via WPI/CPI-linked formulas, so some margin impact is expected, mainly in coal where HSD is a major cost.
Coal MDO pricing is contracted per tonne: about INR500 per tonne at Siarmal and about INR1,100 per tonne at Pachhwara.
Q4 mining margin fell temporarily because about 6 Mt of coal is stuck at Siarmal due to delayed government evacuation and rake unavailability.
Management stated 90% of the last 20 years' revenue came from national government and other states, and only 10% from the Madhya Pradesh state government.

qa_highlights.question: Will MDO revenue and profitability be shared quarterly, and what is the profitability outlook after the coal handling plant capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO revenue and profitability will be shared quarterly. Revenue is projected at about INR2,500 crores in FY27 and INR4,000 crores by FY29, with similar margins to be assumed; no monetisation plan for the subsidiaries is announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected InvIT distribution after the transfers, given lower distributions from Alpha?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said transfer timing changed in FY26 and distributions are envisaged in slide 24; FY26 Shrem and Alpha dividend and interest income was INR64.5 crores, with total distributions close to INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the equity structure, IRR and commissioning timeline for the transmission and solar projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Investors would put in about 85% of equity during construction with DBL 15%; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR high-teens for both. SPVs are formed, lender in-principle approvals obtained, and commissioning is about 2 years from start.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone receivables rise to INR1,783 crores despite lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores of Jal Jeevan Mission final 10% payments, which depend on hydro testing, are pending; they will be paid partly in Q1 and partly in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does coal margin trend, given FY25 blended margin around 26% vs 23% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed a 24-25% stabilised range is the right base, with improvement as volumes scale and the coal handling plant comes online.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pass-through for the raw material escalation from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are linked to WPI and CPI, so pass-through is partial; NHBF is lobbying the government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and what drives the interest cost trend?

540048|2026-03.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.

540061|2026-09.headline: Bigbloc Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~23% YoY to INR 83 crore and EBITDA ~74% to INR 3 crore, with October the record sales month.

EBITDA rose 74% YoY to about INR 3 crore, with margin up 116 bps to 3.98%, while the net loss widened to about INR 2.75 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was about INR 162 crore (+31%), EBITDA about INR 10 crore (margin 5.93%, +334 bps) and net loss about INR 3.5 crore. Management said input costs rose 8-10% and only 5-7% has been passed on so far, with the balance targeted for the next quarter.

segments.commentary: About 87-88% of H1 FY27 volume; manufactured at all 4 plants. Management said red bricks are about 10-15% costlier than AAC blocks, with conversion ongoing.

segments.name: AAC panels
segments.commentary: About 5-6% of H1 FY27 turnover; made at one plant. New orders include AdaniConneX data centre in Hyderabad, bullet train stations, ITC, Foxconn and Embassy Group work.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 5-6% of H1 FY27 turnover; in-house manufacturing started in Q1 FY27 after white-labelling. Plant utilisation is low; management sees potential revenue of about INR 20-25 crore.

Input cost pass-through: the 5-7% differential is to be passed on in the upcoming quarter; further increases to be passed on as H2 demand is seasonally stronger.
Operational efficiency measures (electric forklifts, boiler automation) expected to improve EBITDA margin by about 2-3%, completed in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Further capacity expansion to be decided in the next 1-2 quarters, as utilisation is at 95%+ in some plants.
Gradual price revisions planned across markets while staying competitive.
capex_capacity: Utilisation was 68.74% in H1 FY27 versus about 56-57% in H1 FY26; management said October 2026 was the highest monthly turnover and volume ever.

Boiler automation under way at 3 plants, expected to be completed by the next quarter.

Coal and transport costs rose and drove the increase in other operating expenses in Q2.
Industry average realisation is about INR 3,500-3,600 per cubic metre; management says realisations fell in FY26 and are now being improved.

540073|2026-03.headline: BLS International FY26 revenue rose 37% to INR2,998 crores and EBITDA 30% to INR819 crores, with Q4 PAT up 29% to INR187 crores.
540073|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's highest-ever year on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by Visa application volumes, new contract wins and higher net revenue per application. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR815 crores and EBITDA 17% to INR204 crores, with Visa & Consular volumes up 10% and Digital revenue up 36%. Digital EBITDA margins are thin (about 7-8%) after the Aadifidelis loan-distribution mix shift, while Visa & Consular margins expanded to about 40%. Management said the West Asia conflict has had a temporary impact on travel but has not dented annual growth, and guided to 20-25% growth on the FY26 base for FY27.

segments.name: Digital Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,158 crores (more than doubled from INR440 crores, +114%) and EBITDA INR81 crores (from INR60 crores), so margin is thin. Q4 revenue INR343 crores (from INR252 crores) and Q4 EBITDA INR24 crores. Growth came from BC/loan distribution (Aadifidelis, acquired Nov 2024) and assisted digital and citizen services.

guidance_outlook: FY27 internal target is 20-25% growth on an increased FY26 base, per Shikhar Aggarwal.

Management said Visa & Consular and Digital will both maintain current margins (about 40% and 7-8% EBITDA respectively), with Digital margins expected to improve over time as more services are implemented.
Management would not give April or Q1 FY27 trading commentary, saying only that business is 'steady' and growing over the same quarter last year.
Effective group tax rate is about 10-12%, possibly rising by about 1 percentage point if Dubai moves its tax rate from 9% to 12%.
Cash to be deployed for capacity expansion and inorganic growth; one acquisition announced and in pipeline, with a further INR2,000 crores of acquisitions mentioned over 4-5 years in an interview.
capex_capacity: UIDAI/Aadhaar passport-style service contract (about INR2,500 crores, 6 years, user-pay per application): Phase I of 40-50 offices rolled out; full rollout expected at 200+ offices, taking 1-1.5 years for full revenue; expected EBITDA margin 15-20%; contracted under BLS International, not E-Services.
Network of 155,000+ touch points and around 45,800 channel partners, described as asset-light.
China operations started about six months ago and are described as steady with further potential.
Management said no further acquisitions in the hotel space (UK hotel), with focus on asset-light models.
demand_pricing: Visa applications processed in FY26: 44.1 lakh vs 37.5 lakh (+18%). Q4 applications 10.8 lakh vs 9.8 lakh (+10%).

Major regions cited: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Algeria, UK, USA, Canada, Singapore, and China (picking up).

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Asia situation hurt the last quarter, and would Q4 have been better without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 EBITDA still grew 17% and FY26 EBITDA 30%, so the impact is temporary; it acknowledged some volume could have come back without the conflict. Q1 FY27 was not guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did applications grow about 10% while Visa revenue grew only 7% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Sudhakar and Gaurav Chugh said net revenue grew about 20% against about 10% application growth, reflecting higher value-added service conversion and better pricing on new contracts; reported revenue is gross of third-party vendor sharing.

qa_highlights.question: How is April and FY27 revenue trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give April commentary and said it is growing steadily; internal FY27 target is 20-25% growth on the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO Amit Sudhakar said cash will go to expansion of existing business and inorganic growth; one acquisition is in the pipeline and a few more are under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic vs inorganic split of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No major new acquisition in FY26; Aadifidelis (acquired Nov 2024) contributed about 25% of revenue, and the rest is comparable with last year.

qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are being considered in both segments: Digital more domestic, Visa & Consular targeting overseas. The Aadhaar contract is too early to size; 15-20% EBITDA margin expected, over 6 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Group effective rate about 10-12%; could rise about 1 point if Dubai's free-zone rate moves from 9% to 12%.

540073|2026-06.headline: BLS International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to INR 891 crores, a record, with EBITDA of INR 252 crores (28.3% margin) and PAT of INR 202 crores.

Digital Services grew 32% to INR 330 crores, with EBITDA up 45% to INR 27 crores. Net cash stood at INR 1,617 crores. 540078|2026-09.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q2 FY27 PAT rose 224% YoY to Rs 610.47 lakhs on 12.41% EBITDA margin; revenue up only 3.67%.
540078|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 9,580.87 lakhs, up 3.67% YoY, while EBITDA rose to Rs 1,188.55 lakhs at a 12.41% margin and PAT reached Rs 610.47 lakhs (6.37% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 19,095.40 lakhs (+7.46% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 2,738.03 lakhs (14.34% margin) and PAT of Rs 1,484.30 lakhs (7.77% margin). Management said the strategy is margin-first, with a shift toward higher-margin niche products, and pointed to IBC entry and a Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition by FY28 without giving a build-up. Management gave no firm IBC revenue, capex or margin figures, and EBITDA margin was about 3.5-4 points lower QoQ.

segments.name: Industrial packaging
segments.commentary: Management put it at about 81.88% of revenue for the period and called it the core business; analysts said it was broadly flat, and management described a very slight dip with focus shifting to higher-margin items.

segments.name: Hospital furniture parts (Furnastra brand, launched 2025)
segments.commentary: About 16.27% of revenue. Management said niche items are now above 16% of mix, up from 13-15%, and about 30% YoY growth; exports are being developed in 18 registered countries.

segments.name: Infrastructure furniture and others
segments.commentary: About 1.86% of revenue. Management called the sales seasonal and said the decline was not a concern.

guidance_outlook: Management targets Rs 1,000 crore annual revenue by FY28. It gave no build-up and said details would be announced shortly; the current run-rate is about Rs 400 crore.
Management said revenue at optimal utilisation from existing capacity is about Rs 425 crore, and said practical utilisation is 85-90%.
The 1,000-litre IBC facility in Khalapur is expected to be operational in Q3 FY27, with most of the impact in Q4. Management said IBC margins will be higher than the core, without quantifying.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 demand to be strong and says the EBITDA margin is sustainable, with improvement targeted but not quantified.
Management said exports should begin commercially this year, after trials and approvals.
capex_capacity: Four facilities with 58 blow moulding machines and 22 injection moulding machines; capacity above 36,000 MTPA.
Average capacity utilisation about 64% in FY26 (one answer said 63%), and about 50%+ on average per another answer; the figures given were inconsistent.
Fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-litre IBCs, expected operational in Q3 FY27. Capital turnover about 15x vs 8-10x for other products. Capex amount and IBC capacity were not disclosed.
Management said no further capex beyond the IBC project is planned for now.
demand_pricing: Management said overall demand is very good, with one or two industries down and the rest strong.
Exports go to USA, Canada and Europe; exports were about 1.5% of revenue in H1 FY27 per management.
Management said realisations should rise under a cost-plus model, but volume growth was not quantified. Management said the focus is on profitability over volume.
Polymers are not hedged; about 90-95% of raw material is bought domestically. Reported margins include no inventory gains.
Management said West Asia tensions have not affected export projects or orders so far.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Rs 1,000 crore FY28 target square with a current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a build-up, saying more plans would be announced soon. It said the target is a basket of plans, not mainly IBC, and that it had not said the capacity was enough without capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ by about 3.5-4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, that double-digit EBITDA is good in the current market, and that it is working to improve further. It did not give a number for the quarter-on-quarter dip.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth, given flat-to-weak revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were stable to slightly up and that low-margin portfolio items were rationalised in favour of higher-margin products, without giving volume figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is IBC on track, and what revenue and margin will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IBC will start in Q3 (through December), margins will be higher than the core, and it would give no revenue or market-size numbers until production begins.

qa_highlights.question: What are H1 vs H2 revenue split and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is generally about 40% and H2 about 60% of annual revenue. FY26 utilisation was about 63-64%, and practical maximum is 85-90%, which would mean about Rs 400-420 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company outsourcing any production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some production is outsourced depending on market conditions, but the share is not considerable and no percentage was given.

risks_watch: FY28 Rs 1,000 crore target looks far from the current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore, and no build-up was given.
IBC start (Q3 FY27), revenue, capex and margins are still undisclosed, and the facility had not started by the call date.
Revenue growth of only 3.67% YoY in Q2 against a large EBITDA gain; the margin dipped QoQ.
Cash balance of Rs 6.07 lakhs against borrowings of Rs 9,648.44 lakhs, with D/E at 0.76x; higher depreciation and interest from new capex could weigh on PAT.
Export commercial revenue is still small (about 1.5% of H1 revenue); exports to Poland and new approvals are yet to show in numbers.
Utilisation figures given on the call were inconsistent (about 50%+, 63%, 64%).

I think double digit EBITDA is a good in this kind of market scenario.

540097|2026-09.headline: GAMCO H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79% to INR254 crore and net profit reached INR38.5 crore, with Q2 PAT of INR6 crore.
540097|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 79% to INR254 crore, already about 84% of FY26 full-year revenue, with EBITDA of INR52.9 crore and net profit of INR38.5 crore versus INR6.5 crore in H1 FY26. Q2 revenue rose 61.7% YoY to INR140.6 crore, but Q2 EBITDA of INR12 crore (9% margin) and PAT of INR6 crore were well below Q1, which management attributed to a one-off strong Q1. Net worth rose 24% in six months to INR206.6 crore and debt-to-equity improved to about 1.6x from 1.7x. Management framed the company as a four-vertical group (equity investments, real estate, logistics, hospitality) shifting from marketing gains toward asset-backed income, with most asset revenues expected from FY28 onward.

segments.name: Equity investments / treasury
segments.commentary: Quoted equity investment of about INR230 crore, including stakes in Swiggy, TrucksUp and Drivers4Me. Management said these listed holdings are the most liquid source of funding for expansion.

segments.name: Real estate (Kolkata, OneWorld)
segments.commentary: 9.7% stake in OneWorld, a 212-acre Lucknow township, invested at about INR19.4 crore and revalued at INR153 crore (unrealised gain about INR134 crore). Kolkata plans 13.5 lakh sq ft of residential launches over 1-2 years; Alipore (Uma Properties) expected to yield about INR250 crore revenue, and Jessore Road JV (Elika Realestate, 45% stake) about INR1,100 crore over 5 years.

segments.name: Warehousing / logistics
segments.commentary: Dankuni, Delhi Road land with 40 lakh sq ft development potential and about INR600 crore capex, targeting 8-10% rental yields. Calcutta 100-125 acre project to deliver 25-30 lakh sq ft; revenue expected from calendar 2028. Visco Advisory warehousing asset sold for INR15.8 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Acquired 33.33% of Blissara Resorts (Port Blair) with INR69 crore post-money valuation; planning a 140-key upper upscale hotel on 11 acres with coastal clearance in place. Construction to start in about a month; revenue expected from about 2030 with 5.5-7 year payback including debt and equity.

guidance_outlook: Blissara hotel: construction starting imminently, operations targeted in 2-2.5 years, revenue hitting top line by about 2030.
Warehousing (Calcutta): revenue expected from calendar 2028, within 1-1.5 years of securing land and approvals; leases under negotiation.
Uma Properties (Alipore residential): revenue expected from about March/April 2028, with a possible one-quarter delay.
Management expects constant revenue from most investments after the March 2028 quarter.

Management said the group will keep about 25% of its portfolio in liquid treasury such as equity markets, and expects construction funding and internal accruals to cover much of the next 3 years of spend.

Hotels targeted to be valued at INR500-600 crore each, with at least INR100 crore revenue per property; operator fee structure of about 2% base fee plus GOP-linked incentive, total under about 8-8.5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Dankuni logistics land: 40 lakh sq ft development potential, capex about INR600 crore.
Calcutta: 13.5 lakh sq ft residential launches over 1-2 years; warehousing 100-125 acres giving 25-30 lakh sq ft immediate supply; construction started on ground.
Port Blair hotel: 140 keys on 11 acres; pipeline in Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya under evaluation.
Analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore funding need over 3-5 years was not disputed by management; funding to come from market borrowing, internal accruals, treasury and asset sales.
Nanak Logistics (63-acre park, Amazon anchor leasing 6.25 lakh sq ft on 20 acres) cited as prior group track record.
demand_pricing: Management cited zero Grade A warehouse supply in Calcutta and limited hotel supply in Port Blair, Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya; no pricing or occupancy data were given.
Warehouse targets: 8-10% rental yields, versus management's view that Tier 1 Grade A warehouses offer about 7-9% returns.
Hotel valuation benchmark cited at 10-16x EBITDA; 40-45% GOP assumed for the hotel.
Management said the Port Blair hotel faces no competition for about 3 years after opening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company expand into factoring, lease financing and security-backed lending, and how does this fit with real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be selective and pursue structured niche deals, not plain-vanilla lending, citing the Shalimar Lake City (OneWorld) revaluation and the Visco Advisory exit as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical will create the most value over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is most excited about hospitality, then warehousing, targeting INR100 crore revenue and INR500-600 crore valuation per hotel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for hospitality and warehousing revenue, and what are the execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blissara revenue starts around 2030 after construction; warehousing revenue from calendar 2028; Alipore residential from about March/April 2028. Monsoon delays were the main constraint, now considered over.

qa_highlights.question: How does revenue recognition work with the hotel operator, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operator takes a 1.5-2.5% base fee on gross revenue plus a share of gross operating profit, with total fees under about 8-8.5%. Payback is about 5.5-7 years including debt and equity; INR69 crore post-money valuation for Blissara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR900-1,500 crore funding requirement be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will use the listed equity treasury (keeping about 25% liquid), market borrowing for construction, internal accruals, and asset liquidation as needed. Management did not confirm the analyst's INR400 crore liquidation estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Who owns the other 55% of the Jessore Road project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three or four other West Bengal real estate developers hold the remaining 55%, chosen for execution capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospitality as landowner/investor rather than operator, and how much control does GAMCO have?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lacks operating experience and prefers global operators, and that development-stage entry captures higher returns (11-12% on Tier 2 land versus 7-9% for Tier 1 warehouses). It said it would provide guidance and strategic input.

risks_watch: Q2 earnings fell sharply from Q1 (EBITDA INR12 crore vs INR41 crore; PAT INR6 crore vs INR32 crore), indicating lumpy income from investment gains.
Funding gap: analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore over 3-5 years versus debt of INR327 crore and debt-to-equity of 1.6x; reliance on market borrowing and asset sales.
Timelines are long: hotel revenue around 2030, warehousing from 2028, Alipore from 2028, with possible further slippage.
Heavy reliance on valuation gains (OneWorld INR134 crore unrealised gain) and on the listed equity book, which is market-sensitive.
Limited operating disclosure on the hotel and warehousing revenue models; stated targets are not yet backed by signed leases or contracts. Management said warehousing leases are being negotiated.

540115|2026-03.headline: LTTS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $305.9 Mn and EBIT margin reached 15.2%, with mid-16% margin targeted by Q4 FY27 or earlier.
540115|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue was $305.9 Mn, up 0.3% YoY and down 1.7% QoQ, as the company exited low-margin work and divested SWC (Smart World). EBIT margin rose 40 bps QoQ to 15.2%, the second straight quarter of expansion, with gross margin up 150 bps QoQ. Management said the restructuring is complete, with about $19 Mn annualised revenue exited in Q4 and no further restructuring costs expected. It advanced the margin aspiration to mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and set a 5-year Lakshya 31 plan of 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance given.

segments.commentary: Q4 EBIT margin 16.1%, up 130 bps QoQ; revenue almost flat QoQ. Over 40% of Q4 large deal wins were in Mobility; management expects growth from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Contributed 36% of FY26 revenue; grew 11% YoY in Q4 and sequentially. EBIT margin 28.7%, steady QoQ. Over 50% of Q4 large deal wins; first $50 Mn+ account reported.

segments.name: Tech (incl. Intelliswift)
segments.commentary: Revenue subdued after exits of non-strategic businesses; EBIT margin 12.6%, up 210 bps QoQ on Intelliswift margin gains and restructuring. FY26 Tech including Intelliswift grew 19.7%.

demand_pricing: Large deal TCV in Q4 was $182 Mn; FY26 large deal wins were $855 Mn, up 40% YoY; average large deal TCV about $200 Mn over six quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SWC divested, and does continuing-ops reporting exclude it for all FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Telco Infra and Cyber were scaled internationally, but Smart Cities could not be taken global because of local-government work. Continuing-ops figures exclude SWC from all periods for like-for-like comparison; mostly India and some international SWC operations were sold. Restructuring is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16%-17% margin a five-year target or achievable sooner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier as an aspiration; 16%-17% is the Lakshya FY31 band to be maintained over five years, not a reduction.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 13%-15% CAGR show up, and when do $100 Mn+ and several-hundred-million accounts emerge?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance. A $50 Mn+ trailing-12-month account was delivered in Q4, the first in a long time. Build-out to $100 Mn accounts is mostly organic and will take time; Alind Saxena now focuses on large deals and growth markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13%-15% CAGR in USD and does the 12.4% historical figure include SWC?
qa_highlights.answer: The 13%-15% is USD-based, and the 12.4% five-year CAGR includes SWC. Reported-currency targets may be added over time.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the six bets and what investment is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 50% of revenue today comes from the six bets; more than 70% expected in five years. Management will hold an Investor Day later in the year with detail. Investment focuses on EI, SDV, connectivity, and physical AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more restructuring, and what is the reason for the $19 Mn exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said the Q4 exceptional charge covers the $19 Mn annualised exit in Europe, Israel and the UK, with no further restructuring costs expected.

qa_highlights.question: Could a 15% margin come as early as H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and did not commit to H2 FY26; margins have improved from the 13.3%-13.6% discussed 2-3 years ago.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting client conversations and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients are asking for productivity pass-through and AI spend is rising. About 60% of staff are trained on AI tools, with the rest due within six months. Management believes LTTS is 6-8 months ahead of competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any M&A planned and would margins take a hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Only tuck-in acquisitions; no large acquisition is planned. Intelliswift's acquisition has performed well, and margins will be kept within the 16%-17% band.

540115|2026-06.headline: LTTS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.5% QoQ in constant currency to $309.9 Mn, with EBIT margin up 50 bps QoQ to 15.7%.
540115|2026-06.overview: LTTS grew revenue 1.5% QoQ and 1.9% YoY in constant currency, to $309.9 Mn (Rs 2,940 crore, +2.9% QoQ, +11.5% YoY in rupee terms). EBIT margin expanded to 15.7%, up 50 bps QoQ and 200 bps YoY, and free cash flow was 153% of net income. Sustainability grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, while Tech declined on a medical program stop and large deals slipping into early Q2. Management reiterated sequential growth in revenue and margins for each quarter and a mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27, but declined to give annual guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs reported FY26 EPS Rs 115.89, about +15%
lower QoQ, mainly hedge losses partly offset by rupee benefit

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 2.3% QoQ, led by Aerospace & Rail and Trucks & Off-Highway; segment margin 15.6%, down slightly on onsite ramp-up of new programs. Management expects revenue and margin to improve sequentially as these programs mature. Europe remains challenging.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY; the most profitable segment with margin of 29.1%, up 40 bps QoQ. Management confirmed double-digit growth for FY27, citing Plant Engineering (Upstream O&G, LNG, Chemicals) and Industrial Products (Data Centers, Electrical Equipment).

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Declined QoQ on a medical program that ended and a new one that was delayed; segment margin 11.5%. Tech is now 30.6% of revenue vs 34.4% a year ago. Management expects a return to growth from Q2, with a significant telecom deal expected to close in early Q2.

guidance_outlook: Sequential improvement in revenue and EBIT margin expected in every quarter of FY27, reconfirmed by the CEO.
Mid-16% EBIT margin targeted on or before Q4 FY27; long-term aspiration of 16-17% EBIT margin.
5-year aspiration of 13-15% revenue CAGR; management declined to give an annual FY27 revenue outlook.
Combined DSO to stay in the 80-85 day range; FCF to be 90-95% of net income for the year (management said Q1 cash conversion of 153% was exceptional).
ETR guided to 26.2% to 26.7%; other income to stay at Q1 levels for the next few quarters due to hedge losses.
Smart World (Tech) disinvestment expected to close in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Opened Europe's first Engineering Intelligence Center in Munich during Q1.
Launched Ainfonix, an Engineering Intelligence platform for process industry clients.
Headcount broadly flat at 23,845; management said it could have grown Sustainability faster with more talent, and it continues to hire there.
Created a team of 100 forward-deployed engineers and a flexible ramp-up model to start work as soon as deals close.
AI patents at 244; total patent count 1,757.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of nearly $100 Mn in Q1; some deals expected to close in Q1 slipped into early Q2. Management said the slippage is not broad-based and is client-specific.
Management said US auto demand is improving and the worst is behind it; Europe OEMs and Tier-1s are under pressure from the Asia/China supply shakeout.
Japan OEMs are looking to use India for engineering and localisation.
Pricing: management said no client has asked for rate cuts recently, and AI-led productivity is partly being passed on to clients to win work in a competitive market.
Management claims a 6-9 month lead over competitors in Engineering Intelligence.
Sustainability pipeline is strong; no pullback seen from clients despite crude price volatility, though Middle East revenue was small and some execution was delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tech decline QoQ, and what differentiates Mobility in a weak auto market?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech fell due to a medical program ending and a new one not starting on schedule; management expects Mobility and Tech to grow in FY27. Mobility differentiation was cited as EV/hybrid lab investments, SDV with AI, and diversification across auto, T&OH, Aero and Rail.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-led large deal sizes and vendor consolidation appear in ER&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said most large deals are now fixed-price or outcome-based and must include process transformation, with AI embedded. Management cited consulting, implementation and owner's-engineer positioning, including a Claude partnership.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF to net income stay at 153%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Q1 was a stellar working-capital quarter; the full-year FCF conversion expected is 90-95% of net income.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI-led productivity hit pricing, and how is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said clients have not asked for rate cuts; productivity gains are partly shared with clients to win bids, and LTTS aims to keep gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth be better than Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year view but committed to growth in Q2, with the timing of the telecom deal and medical deals as key drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tech share of revenue structural, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Tech will not return to its 34% share soon; growth will come more from Sustainability and Mobility. Other income is lower mainly on hedge losses, and the same range is expected for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is crude volatility a risk to Sustainability demand, and what is the Mobility split?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said there was no pullback from Plant Engineering clients and reconfirmed double-digit Sustainability growth for FY27. Mobility is no longer split into sub-segments, and the split will not be provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is the deal slippage broad-based, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said the slippage is not broad-based, with two deals delayed; ramp-ups are tied to the win dates. Management said the pipeline is broad across sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How have client conversations changed amid geopolitical uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said client discussions are mostly focused on market share and AI, with some insulation from the Middle East conflict. Clients are asking whether AI will be net positive for their business, and cost neutrality is a driver.

Europe auto (OEM and Tier-1) demand remains weak, and management said recovery will take time.

540115|2026-09.headline: LTTS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.7% QoQ in constant currency to $317.1M, with EBIT margin at 16.3%, ahead of its mid-16% aspiration.
540115|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached $317.1M (up 2.7% QoQ and 4.8% YoY in constant currency, continuing operations), and INR 3,040 crore (up 3.4% QoQ, 12.1% YoY). EBIT margin widened 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, and management said the mid-16% aspiration was reached a couple of quarters early. Large deal TCV was $203M with over 50% AI-led, and management said the USD100M shortfall from last quarter's target would be recovered over Q3 and Q4. Reported net income of INR 548 crore included a one-time INR 165 crore gain from the SWC divestment, which is now complete.

financial_highlights.change: +53.7% QoQ; +66.8% YoY; includes INR 165 crore one-time SWC gain
vs 77 days in Q1; guided range 80 to 85 days
vs INR 3,394 crore at end Q1

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue up 2.3% QoQ, with growth from Auto North America, Aero and Rail, and Trucks and Off-highway. Auto Europe remained muted; management expects it to recover next year. Auto is about 50% of Mobility revenue. Margin 16.9%.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Up 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ; now about 30% of revenue per the CFO (38% per the later AI-revenue answer, which conflicts). Nearly half of Q2 large deal wins were here. Margin 29.5%. Management says it is on track for another double-digit growth year.

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Described as stable. Tech Infra and Semcon were strong, Media steady. A global telecom equipment AI program began ramping this quarter. Margin 12%, up 50 bps QoQ. Management expects Tech to be muted in Q3, with Medtech recovery in Q4.

segments.name: Engineering Intelligence (EI)
segments.commentary: Annualized EI-led revenue of $120M in Q2, which management said is about 9.5% of revenue. Headcount was 24,035 and more than 16,000 engineers were upskilled in AI. Over 50% of Q2 large deal wins were AI-led.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than H1, both QoQ and YoY, per management.
Near-term EBIT margin expected around mid-16% levels; aspiration to maintain it.
Long-term aspiration: 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with 16% to 17% EBIT margin over 3 to 5 years.
Wage hike effective Q3, expected impact of 50 to 80 bps on margin; margin guidance stated as inclusive of this.
Effective tax rate guided at 26% to 26.5%.
Management expects to recover the roughly USD100M shortfall from the prior quarter in Q3 and Q4 to keep a USD200M-per-quarter deal pace.
Tech expected muted in Q3; Medtech growth expected from Q3 or Q4; Systems and Platforms growth to accelerate from Q4.
capex_capacity: Set up a dedicated Data Center Engineering business line covering AI infrastructure, servers, storage, ODMs and OEMs.
Launched a new EI lab with NVIDIA for physical AI applications across manufacturing, robotics and supply chain.
Investment in Munich and an EI center to target European auto work.
Headcount rose marginally from 23,845 in Q1 to 24,035 in Q2.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of $203M across segments in Q2, with over 50% AI-led. Order backlog and pipeline both up YoY; pipeline up more than 25% YoY.
Offshore mix 55.9%; fixed-price mix 35.6%, rising toward higher-value and outcome-based engagements.
Average deal tenures have lengthened slightly. Management cited roughly 5 to 7 years for a $100M deal, 4 to 5 years for $50M, about 3 years for $25M.
Management says it charges a premium for AI-led work but declined to quantify AI-led margins by service line.
Rupee realized at 95.9 per dollar in Q2, depreciating 1.09% QoQ.
Attrition range-bound at 14.7%.
Europe auto remains weak; management said there is little Middle East exposure in oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: How has Sustainability volatility come down, and how much revenue is long-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split Sustainability into four areas (Oil and Gas/Chemicals, FMCG, Energy Automation, Industrial Machinery and Building Tech), built digital twin and AI solutions, and said large deals from last year are now converting to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East situation affecting oil and gas or overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East business is very small and it is not seeing significant impact; work is focused on the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will European auto recover next year, and is it an industry-wide turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Europe auto to stabilize in the next 6 to 9 months and grow again in 9 to 12 months, as European OEMs rebase and India-based providers replace local vendors. Auto Europe is about 50% of the auto portion of Mobility, and the company does not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 78 days comfortable, or is there room to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is comfortable at 78 days, well below the 80 to 85 day guided range, and expects to operate around this level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the SWC divestment affect the reported numbers, and what is the run rate from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR 165 crore was a one-time gain. From Q3 only continuing operations will be reported, with the SWC operating line of about $36M excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why are clients converting deals to revenue now, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AI capex across chips, software, industrials, telecom and infrastructure, clients focusing on growth rather than cost cuts, and LTTS being 9 to 12 months ahead of peers on AI, which it says is gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable margins, and what is the Q4 exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said near-term margins should be taken at around mid-16% EBIT, with levers from mix, AI and productivity, net of the wage hike. Management did not give a Q4 exit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike impact, and what does H2 growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the wage hike in Q3 would have a 50 to 80 bps margin impact. Management said H2 will be better than H1 both QoQ and YoY, without a quarterly number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $120M annualized EI revenue was recognized in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the $120M is annualized, so about $30M per quarter. Most AI deal wins have not yet gone into operation, and the company will report AI-led revenue quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI-led revenue defined, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue counts deliverables where a significant part is created using the AI stack. Management declined to quantify AI-led profitability, but said AI is a margin lever.

Wage hike of 50 to 80 bps in Q3 may pressure margins if growth lags.
H2 growth acceleration depends on converting the USD100M-plus deal backlog; most AI deal wins are not yet operational.

540133|2026-03.headline: ICICI Pru Life FY26 VNB rose 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9%.
540133|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed absolute VNB growth of 10.9% to ₹26.29bn and VNB margin expansion to 24.7% (from 22.8%), while APE grew just 2.2% to ₹106.41bn. Retail protection was the standout, up 32.3% for the year and 60.5% in Q4, offsetting weak agency, direct, linked and annuity lines. Profit after tax rose 34.6% to ₹16bn, helped by a ₹1.14bn gain on sale of ICICI Pension Fund Management Company; excluding it, PAT grew 25%. EV operating assumption changes (GST input-tax-credit loss, persistency) and a ₹2.64bn persistency variance (mainly the 100% premium back annuity) pulled RoEV down to 11.9%. Management said West Asia disruption hurt March new business across all lines except protection, and it deferred Ind-AS adoption by a year via forbearance.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 32.3% YoY in FY26 and 60.5% in Q4; 13% of addressable population covered. Protection mix rose 2.2pp to 17.9% of VNB mix.

segments.name: Group protection
segments.commentary: Up 7.1% YoY; group term +14.6%, credit life +1.8%. Group business overall +14.5%, 18.3% of APE.

segments.name: Linked (ULIP)
segments.commentary: APE up 1.6% YoY; two-year CAGR 14.2%. Focus on high sum assured ULIP to cushion market volatility.

segments.name: Non-linked savings
segments.commentary: APE grew 15.4% YoY for nine months but declined YoY in Q4 as a prior-year Q4 launch normalised; full year roughly flat. Par:non-par roughly 2:1.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Four-year CAGR about 20%; stabilised at about 7% of retail mix. Heavy single-pay skew and 100% premium back product drove persistency issues.

segments.name: Group Funds
segments.commentary: Grew 26% YoY.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹26.86bn; with direct, 47.4% of retail APE. Growth weak on high annuity base, but improving sequentially through the year.

segments.name: Direct channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹14.30bn; growth lagged on base effects. Focus on NRI via GIFT City and online channel.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 3.6% YoY; 29.8% of APE. 53 bank partnerships with access to 26,400+ branches.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 23.4% YoY; 13.2% of APE. Over 1,500 non-bank partnerships.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 growth number given; management called the environment volatile and said it is too early to commit.
Long-term RoEV expected at 13-14%, depending on yield curve and VNB growth; RoEV to become less significant once Ind-AS is adopted.
Management said VNB margin of 24.7% (with persistency and mortality/expense assumptions now set) is the baseline going forward.
Ind-AS go-live deferred by a year via forbearance; current-year results remain on existing I-GAAP with Ind-AS as alternate financials.
Would reprice non-par products if the yield curve moves down; no en masse repricing so far, only cohort-level changes (1-3% at some peers).
capex_capacity: Distribution: 2.42 lakh+ advisers, 53 bank partnerships, 1,500+ non-bank partnerships.
Agency strategy centres on micro-market-led branch expansion and technology/analytics productivity tools.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict hurt new business in March 2026 across all products except protection, per management.
Industry retail sum assured grew 2.5x in the post-GST-reform period versus pre-reform; GST removed 18% on retail protection.
Non-par sales are constrained because bank FD rates are steep relative to G-Sec-linked pricing, so customers switch products.
Management said it has not cut prices en masse; the yield curve benefit was retained rather than passed to customers.

Persistency: 61st month decline attributed to a regulatory definition change; 25th month decline seen as spillover from 13th month, largely annuity-driven. Non-linked 13th-month persistency fell from 86.8% to 73.2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth strategy and non-par outlook, and what is the par/non-par mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth outlook not committed given volatility. Par:non-par mix roughly 2:1 for the year, with some quarters higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency experience built into VNB margin assumptions, and what about surrender value regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency is reviewed at year-end; permanent changes go into assumptions and temporary ones run through variances. Early surrender-value product experience is not yet showing a material difference after 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is agency growing slowly, and how will it be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency was held back by a high annuity base in the prior year. The 3-year CAGR is about 12-13%; micro-market-led agency strategy is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Did the West Asia war affect new business, and how does demand differ across products?
qa_highlights.answer: March new business was hit across the board except protection. Management declined to quantify the impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ind-AS transition plan and its capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forbearance sought for one year, citing awaited joint expert group clarity on CSM inputs. Solvency stays on the existing basis (227%) until RBC is implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 2.5pp economic variance uplift in VNB margin, and was pricing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield curve gains were held in economic assumptions, while product repricing sits in new business profile. Pricing was not materially changed; cost efficiencies were used to hold prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EV split between VIF and net worth reclassified?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder share of MTM on policyholder-fund assets and derivatives moved from net worth to VIF to align with market practice. Total EV is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.64bn persistency variance related to FY26 VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost none of it relates to FY26 business; it is entirely back-book.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not aware of discussions beyond data requests from the regulator; distributor remuneration talks are continuous.

risks_watch: APE growth of 2.2% against market growth of 10-11% (two-year CAGR ~7-8% vs market 10-11%); share loss risk.

GST input-tax-credit loss and pricing lag; operating assumption change of -0.5% of opening EV.

Possible regulatory commission cuts; management gave no sensitivity.
Ind-AS transition and RBC solvency regime changes; the next-year forbearance outcome is open.

540133|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru Life Q1 FY27: VNB up 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn at 26.7% margin, driven by retail protection growth of 60.4%.

Growth was led by protection: sum assured up 31.8% to ₹4.90 trn and protection APE up 45.7%, while savings APE rose only 5.8% and non-linked APE fell about 9.5% as fixed deposits attracted customers. Management repeatedly stated there is no margin target and no formal guidance, and that absolute VNB growth is the focus.

segments.commentary: Grew 37.8% YoY; MFI credit life recovered after a long slowdown, non-MFI momentum continued.

segments.commentary: Savings APE ₹15.40 bn, up 5.8% YoY; savings share of mix fell to 72.1% from 78.1%. Linked APE up 6.4%; non-linked including annuity broadly flat at ₹4.94 bn; group funds up 42.2%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: APE up 2% YoY to ₹4.63 bn, improved from negative growth in prior quarters; channel shifting to higher sum assured and protection.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 5.6% YoY, 27.4% of APE; management attributes this to partner-bank recalibration.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% YoY, 14.6% of APE; management cites a near 20% five-year CAGR and no single partner above 5%.

segments.commentary: Grew 38.8% YoY, 22.9% of APE.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no VNB growth or margin guidance; it said margin is not a fixation and absolute VNB growth is the goal.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin, and is the GST input tax credit drag still affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dhiren Salian said the margin was largely product mix; the non-availability of input tax credit continues for one more quarter (Q2) before entering the base from Q3. He did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-par not selling, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-income alternatives, mainly fixed deposits with high sticker rates, are more attractive to customers. Non-par is not being avoided and is repriced as conditions allow, but the pickup depends on those alternatives easing.

qa_highlights.question: Will Standard Chartered remain an open-architecture partner after Prudential's change in promoter status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Standard Chartered has been a 10-year partner, that both sides value it, and that ICICI Bank is the largest single channel at about 15% of business with no other distributor above 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How does expense management look, and what is the ITC drag in rupees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-premium is up on the input tax credit loss, partly offset by productivity and AI/ML gains. It did not quantify the ITC impact and said the schedules would show the GST component. It said EOM is well within the cap, without disclosing the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any VNB growth guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to give VNB growth guidance, including the 20-25% range an analyst proposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Prudential promoter-to-investor reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Prudential holds just under 22%. The board approved its request to reclassify as investor, and the company has submitted it to IRDAI, awaiting its response. Management said no sell-down is required under its reading of the rules.

540133|2026-09.headline: H1-FY27 VNB rose 22.3% to ₹12.83 billion, with VNB margin at 26.0% on a protection-led mix shift.

Consumer and Industrial (C&I) grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and rose to 43% of revenue from 37%, led by wires and cables (up 50% to Rs 340 crore). 540136|2026-06.headline: HPL Electric Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.26% on raw-material inflation, with metering margins roughly halved.
540136|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, the highest-ever Q1, while EIA grew 9% to ₹63 cr and PAT rose to ₹19 cr. Consumer & Industrial (C&I) hit a record ₹278 cr (+55% YoY, ~54% of revenue) and Metering & Systems grew ~17% to ₹234 cr. EBITDA margin moderated to 12.26% as metals, industrial plastics and semiconductors inflated after February 2026 due to West Asia geopolitical disruption, and depreciation from recent capacity investments weighed on PAT. Management guided that pricing and mix actions are under way, with margin recovery expected over one to three quarters if input costs ease.

segments.name: Consumer & Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Record ₹278 cr revenue, +55% YoY, ~54% of Q1 revenue. Wire & cable ₹146 cr (+79%) already above 40% of FY26 full-year wire & cable revenue; lighting +78%; industrial switchgear ₹56 cr (+19%).

segments.name: Metering & Systems (smart metering)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹234 cr, ~+17% YoY. Order book ~₹3,200 cr as of 7 Aug 2026, with metering & systems over 96% of orders. Metering margin fell roughly 50% in Q1 per management, driven by industrial plastics and metals.

guidance_outlook: Management expects C&I and smart metering to both deliver revenue growth; C&I visibility of 12-18 months described as strong, with high double-digit growth expected.

Current margin levels described as a conservative baseline; recovery could take an extra quarter, with C&I margins possibly back to target by Q3 FY27 if copper and other input prices stay at current levels.
If the Middle East situation eases and crude falls, management said margins of 16-17% could be restored, and it aims to grow margins further.
Smart metering visibility of 2-3 years cited; pace depends on AMISP execution. About 7 crore meters installed nationally to date.

Capex expected to be mainly maintenance (tools, dies) for metering; new projects may need capex but are expected to carry separate revenue streams. Analyst suggested ₹50-100 cr for the next year or two; management did not confirm.
capex_capacity: Metering capacity is in place after recent investments; future metering capex is mainly maintenance (tools and dies).
Automation: recently commissioned a new MCB machine that replaces 44 workers, producing ~18,000 MCBs a day, with 7-8 such machines installed across factories. Stated ROI is 3-4 years.
Seven factories, three tool rooms and over 100 injection moulding machines; electronics manufacturing described as large and internally integrated.
Backward integration in metering: relays and some critical components are not yet made in-house; management said work is in progress under a Chinese-partner MoU but gave no timeline.
Water meters launched; gas metering considered as a future category, with no commitment.
demand_pricing: Smart metering: ~7 crore meters installed nationally per latest official figure, against a first-phase target of 25 crore. Management said the Adani group's acquisition of Intellis Smart is positive, as HPL is an approved vendor for both companies.

Smart meter pricing: contracts are fixed-price; semiconductor lead times up to 52 weeks. Management expects to pass on some price increases on new tenders, but acknowledged competitive pressure from AMISPs.
C&I pricing: wire & cable has had a couple of price increases, passed on quickly; lighting saw its first price increase in ~7-8 years; switchgear pass-through is slower.
Distribution: 900+ authorised dealers and 85,000+ retailers; 'one consumer one family' scheme incentivises cross-selling.
Data centre cables: HPL does not have the full range yet; it plans to launch products with international certifications around May-June 2027.
Exports: a Middle East utility recently approved HPL's meter; DEKRA-certified MCB and lab support sales in ~55 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margins fell from ~38% to ~30%. What steps are being taken to restore margins, and is hedging used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to input costs rising from February due to West Asia conflict. Long-term contracts, alternate materials and design changes, and price pass-through are being used; semiconductors are bought at order time, while metals and plastics cannot be hedged. Metering margins fell about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Will smart meter price increases pass through on new tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is asking AMISPs for price increases on new orders, but competition limits this. Pricing power depends on being a trusted, quality-focused supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wire & cable growth sustainable, and what is being done in channel expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper tonnage is up 1.5-2x from a year ago, with growth across solar, industrial, real estate and retail. Management is spending on BTS marketing, a third-party last-mile sales team and dealer/retailer expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How is the AMISP consolidation (Adani/Intellis) affecting order flow, and is there an industry tender slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Intellis acquisition positive as HPL is approved by both. Orders are placed on 3-4 month requirements, not multi-year locks. Management said ~25 crore meters' first phase is largely tendered and enough orders exist for the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin baseline for new orders, and when do C&I margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Q1 margins are a conservative baseline; new metering orders have supply lead times of several months, so price relief comes with a lag. C&I margins could recover by Q3 FY27 if input prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex rise, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering capex is mainly maintenance. New projects would carry separate revenue streams, and details will come later. Analyst's ₹50-100 cr estimate was not confirmed.

financial_highlights.change: moderated YoY; exact prior-year figure not stated
down from ~38% last year; not confirmed by management

risks_watch: Metering margin pressure: management said metering margins fell roughly 50% in Q1 on industrial plastics and metals, and new orders carry supply lead times, so price relief lags.
Pricing pass-through on smart meter tenders depends on competitive AMISP negotiations; management said price increases are being requested but not secured.
Semiconductor lead times of up to 52 weeks and metals/plastics that cannot be hedged keep input-cost exposure open, with West Asia developments outside management control.
AMISP consolidation (Adani acquiring Intellis Smart, and reported interest in a meter OEM) could shift order flow; management did not comment on the second item.

Execution pace of smart meter orders depends on AMISPs; management gave no firm quarterly order inflow or tender timing, and the ~₹3,200 cr order book is said to be stable at around ₹3,000 cr over recent quarters.

Depreciation from recent capacity investments and higher manpower costs (Haryana minimum wage up ~40% in May) continue to weigh on profit conversion; relay and critical metering components are not yet made in-house with no timeline given.
key_quotes: Our highest ever first quarter revenue and remained above 500 cr level despite Q1 typically being a seasonally light Quarter.
there's a single point like on on the cost of materials that has gone up and that has gone up mainly from February onwards because of the the West Asia conflict
So I think the next 12 to 18 months will be very strong the the cable and wire segment has been we've been growing well well above
The only thing there the pace of sales depends a lot on execution.

It declined to give numbers on AMISP tender flow, the Adani-related OEM news, backward-integration timelines and capex size.
