540136|2026-09.headline: HPL Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.74%.
540136|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, the first quarter above ₹600 crore, taking H1 revenue to ₹1,124 crore (up 37%). Consumer and Industrial (C&I) revenue grew 64% to ₹337 crore and was about 55% of quarterly revenue, while Metering and Systems grew 18% to ₹271 crore. Q2 EBITDA rose 8% to ₹71 crore and PAT rose to ₹23 crore, but the EBITDA margin fell to 11.74% from 12.26% in Q1 on input cost inflation and mix. The Board also gave in-principle approval to evaluate a restructuring, possibly a scheme of arrangement to separate one or more businesses.

segments.name: Consumer and Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹337 crore, up 64% YoY and about 55% of quarterly revenue; H1 ₹615 crore, up 60%. Management said full-year C&I revenue should comfortably exceed the ₹1,000 crore it had indicated.

segments.name: Wires and cables (within C&I)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹178 crore, up 159% YoY; H1 ₹324 crore, about 95% of FY26 full-year revenue. Growth is now mostly volume-led, with telecom, real estate, retail, panel builders and OEMs cited as drivers.

segments.name: Lighting and switchgear (within C&I)
segments.commentary: Lighting grew 59% YoY, domestic switchgear 43% YoY, and industrial switchgear 29% QoQ. Management plans a revamped lighting range around ELECRAMA in February; fans are a new category with pan-India launch targeted for summer 2027.

segments.name: Metering and Systems
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹271 crore, up 18% YoY and 14% QoQ; H1 ₹509 crore, up 17%. Order book of ₹2,700 crore gives visibility beyond the current year, though quarterly conversion depends on customer schedules.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to be much better than H1 in revenue across C&I and smart metering; FY28 sales plan is almost ready.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise around 12% (CFO: full-year 12–12.5%), with improvement later if geopolitical conditions ease.
C&I cost increases to be largely passed on by the close of Q3 FY27, with a one-to-two-month lag and further price increases lined up after Diwali.
Metering margins described as decent at 15%+ at current volumes, though fixed contracts prevent pass-through of input cost increases.
Retail outlets targeted to reach 100,000 by March 2027, and C&I doubling targeted over three years.
Smart water meter numbers expected next year (FY28) after pilots and approvals; specialty cable commercial production expected around June 2027.
Management says the company is growing well above industry figures and is prioritising balance sheet ratios (inventory, debtors) and working capital.
risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 11.74%; recovery depends on pass-through of C&I price increases after Diwali and on geopolitical input costs.
Metering contracts are fixed-price, so metal, plastic and electronics inflation cannot be passed on; a further drop in tender prices could weigh on margins.
Smart meter installation delays and AMISP payment timing; deployment pace depends on government push and a 2028 deadline for phase one.
Working capital: management flagged stock and debtor ratios as a priority, implying pressure on cash conversion.
Restructuring (possible demerger) is at an early evaluation stage with no timeline; details and value impact are unknown.
Wire and cable growth will taper in percentage terms because the Q3–Q4 FY26 base is high.
Export ramp-up is slowed by supply-chain and freight delays to Africa and the Middle East.
540136|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume growth and the C&I platform, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly said 12% EBITDA should stabilise and was evasive on restructuring specifics and timing.
key_quotes: Revenue from operations grew 40% year-on-year to 608 crores, our highest ever quarterly revenue and the first time we have crossed 600 crore level.
I don't see the margins going down further from here, but at least in the C&I part it should start coming up.
So I think that definitely helps us a lot.
Whatever happens, it will be good for the shareholders, and it would definitely unlock a good amount of value for them.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins normalise in the second half, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin should stabilise around 12% and, when asked, confirmed a full-year range of 12–12.5%; C&I cost increases to be largely passed on by close of Q3 with a 1–2 month lag, and metering contracts are fixed so inflation cannot be passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Adani's takeover of IntelliSmart and the smart meter tender landscape on HPL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it positive: HPL is an approved vendor with Adani and EESL and a preferred vendor with each independent AMISP; quantities to flow through Adani, including EESL's extra quantities. Management expects 15–20% growth in smart meter volumes and says the 2028 deadline for phase one drives demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is aggressive L1 pricing in tenders sustainable, and what is the breakeven volume for metering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aggressive pricing has not been sustainable historically and fewer established players will remain; current volumes give decent margins of 15%+, and the recent margin pressure is seen as a one-off from geopolitical material and supply-chain inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation across wires and cables and metering, and is further investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering utilisation about 70% with flexible capacity; wires and cables about 80% after adding 7–8 machines in six months, with more ordered. A 3-year capacity and new-product evaluation is under way, which would entail capex not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book dip and for the rest of FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹2,700 crore metering order book is not material at 2,500–3,000 crore levels, with over 2 years of revenue visibility. H2 FY27 expected to be much better than H1; C&I to comfortably exceed the ₹1,000 crore indication (already ₹615 crore in H1); FY28 sales plan almost ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope and timing of the restructuring and the smart water meter opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: On restructuring, management said it is an enabling provision at evaluation stage with no timeline, typically a demerger of B2B and B2C businesses, and it would unlock shareholder value. Smart water meters: pilots are done and approvals are pending, with meaningful numbers expected next year (FY28).

capex_capacity: Metering capacity utilisation around 70%, after heavy capex over the last two and a half years; management says capacity is flexible and has upside if government pushes implementation toward the 2028 phase-one deadline.
Wires and cables flexible manufacturing capacity utilisation around 80%; 7 to 8 new machines added in the last six months, with more machines ordered on a staggered basis.
Management is evaluating capacity additions, including new wire and cable products, over the next 3 years; this would entail capex but is under evaluation with no amount disclosed.
Specialty cable commercial production expected around June 2027; full business plan and investment details to be shared once in place, likely in 2 to 3 years.
Lighting revamp with new smart lighting range targeted for ELECRAMA in February; fans to be addressed pan-India from summer 2027.
demand_pricing: Metering order book of ₹2,700 crore as on 2 Nov 2026; management said the absolute level (₹2,500–3,000 crore) is not material, with over 2 years of revenue visibility and monthly order inflows.
C&I order book reflects only about 15–20 days of orders; daily order flow described as healthy.

C&I cost increases partly passed on in Q2, with further price increases lined up after Diwali; pass-through expected largely by close of Q3 FY27 with a one-to-two-month lag. Lighting prices have stabilised and started rising after falling for about four years.

Wire and cable growth now mostly volume-led after earlier copper-price-driven value growth; demand cited from real estate, telecom, retail, panel builders and OEMs. Percentage growth to taper because Q3–Q4 FY26 base is high.

Metering fixed-price contracts prevent pass-through of metal, plastic and electronics inflation; current metering margins described as decent at 15%+. Management expects 15–20% smart meter volume growth.
Exports: first good African order received including advance; Africa and Middle East deliveries slowed by supply-chain and freight delays; FTAs expected to help.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 11.74% from 12.26% in Q1, and management guides full-year 12-12.5%, so margin recovery to above Q1 levels is not guided; pass-through of C&I cost increases lags 1-2 months and metering contracts are fixed-price.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Wires and cables utilisation is about 80% after 7-8 machines added in six months with more ordered staggered, and metering is at about 70%, but no amount is disclosed for the new-product/capacity evaluation over 3 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 FY27 much better than H1 (H1 revenue ₹1,124 crore, up 37%), C&I to comfortably exceed ₹1,000 crore (H1 already ₹615 crore), and smart meter volumes to grow 15-20% against a ₹2,700 crore metering order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Wire and cable utilisation is about 80% with more machines ordered, but the 3-year capacity evaluation has no amount disclosed and management has already spent heavily over the last two and a half years, so the announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: C&I FY27 revenue guided to comfortably exceed ₹1,000 crore against ₹615 crore in H1, which implies a revenue beat on that segment, but margin guidance was cut to 12-12.5% and metering is fixed-price.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins fell to 11.74% in Q2 and recovery depends on C&I price pass-through after Diwali and on geopolitical input costs, while metering fixed-price contracts cannot pass through inflation and export deliveries to Africa and the Middle East are slowed by freight delays.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Revamped lighting and smart lighting range is targeted for ELECRAMA in February, and a pan-India fan launch is targeted for summer 2027, with specialty cable commercial production around June 2027.

rows.label: Smart water meters commercial numbers in FY28
rows.why: Pilots are done and approvals are pending, with meaningful numbers expected next year (FY28).

rows.label: Restructuring / possible demerger of B2B and B2C businesses
rows.why: Board gave in-principle approval to evaluate a scheme of arrangement, which management described as an enabling provision at evaluation stage with no timeline.

rows.label: C&I price increases after Diwali
rows.when: Post-Diwali, by close of Q3 FY27
rows.why: C&I cost increases are to be largely passed through by close of Q3 FY27 with a 1-2 month lag, and further price increases are lined up after Diwali.

tone.note: Management was confident on C&I growth, metering order visibility and smart meter demand, but cautious on margins (12-12.5% full year) and evasive on restructuring timing; analysts pressed on margin normalisation, aggressive L1 tender pricing and capacity needs.

540153|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 37.3% YoY to ₹4,116 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5%, while raw-material and energy inflation remain a pass-through challenge.
540153|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income grew 31.1% YoY to ₹2,975 crores, with EBITDA up 13.7% to ₹371 crores (12.5% margin) and PAT up 20.5% to ₹210 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA rose 30.8% to ₹598 crores, helped by Europe's best-ever quarter (EBITDA €21.9 million, 20.5% margin). Management said full-year standalone RMC rose 1.5 percentage points to 66.82% of revenue, and that ₹73.7 crores of aluminium and steel inflation was not passed through, which would have lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% from 12.6%. Management expects Q1 FY27 to stay volatile on energy and metal costs and sees better numbers from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: ₹14,720 crores (EBITDA ₹2,090 crores, 14.2% margin; PAT ₹952 crores, 6.5% margin)

segments.name: Europe (Endurance Overseas)
segments.commentary: Q4 turnover €106.9 million (+33.6% YoY; ~7.4% excluding Stöferle) and EBITDA €21.9 million (20.5% margin, +49.1%). FY26 turnover €391.7 million (+28.9%) and EBITDA €72.4 million (18.5% margin).

segments.name: Stöferle (acquired April 2025)
segments.commentary: Q4 turnover €21 million, EBITDA €4.9 million, net result €2.6 million. FY26 (since acquisition) turnover €82.1 million, EBITDA €17.9 million, net result €8 million.

segments.name: Maxwell (battery management and electronics)
segments.commentary: FY26 record turnover ₹162 crores vs ₹70 crores in FY25; supplied 350,000 BMS units. Q4 EBITDA hit by a ₹6 crore provision on Hero Electric inventory; management says gross margin is safe excluding it. FY26 new orders ₹56 crores, cumulative ₹247 crores per annum.

segments.name: Brakes and ABS
segments.commentary: About 280,000 single-channel ABS units sold in FY26; management guides growth of 100-150% in FY27. Capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum with SOP expected September 2026. Dual-channel ABS SOP June 2026 for Bajaj Auto (120,000 units per annum), with a second 120,000-unit program in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Suspension
segments.commentary: Inverted front fork output to rise from 60,000 to 75,000 units per month by June 2026 and to 100,000 by end FY27. Demand is also rising for mono shocks.

segments.name: Aluminium castings and forging
segments.commentary: AURIC Shendra new orders translate into peak business potential of ₹513 crores per annum (peak FY29; plant expected to cross ₹200 crores in FY27). Chakan demand from Tata Motors and Mahindra rising 35-40%. A fifth aluminium forging press is being added at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, with SOP in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Alloy wheels (AURIC Bidkin and Chakan)
segments.commentary: Crossed 100,000 wheel sales in January 2026. Total capacity now 48 lakh wheel sets per annum. Bidkin is targeted to reach about ₹600 crores per annum sales by end Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Battery packs (Talegaon, Pune)
segments.commentary: Order for 2W EV battery packs worth ~₹300 crores per annum, potentially ₹350-360 crores. SOP planned for the last week of May 2026. Management said it could reach ₹600 crores per annum next FY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India capex expected to be similar to FY26 (~₹800 crores in FY26, up from ₹600 crores); automation is a key focus.
Q1 FY27 expected to be volatile on energy, aluminium and oil costs; management expects much better numbers from Q2 FY27 if the conflict eases.
Standalone EBITDA margin would have been 13.3% in FY26 excluding the ₹73.7 crore non-value-add aluminium and steel inflation.
Management aims to raise 4W share of revenue from about 6% in FY26 to 10% 'soon'.
Maharashtra incentive raised to ₹858 crores from ₹600 crores, to be availed over about seven years via state GST refund.
Chennai disc brake plant: Royal Enfield SOP July 2026, other OEMs from Q3 FY27. Tata Motors 4W drum brake and driveshaft SOPs in Q2 FY27 / June 2026.
capex_capacity: ABS capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum (existing 6.4 lakh), SOP September 2026, to proceed irrespective of final regulations.
Chennai brake plant: 3 million disc brake assemblies and 4 million discs per annum; Royal Enfield SOP July 2026. Group target is 7.6 million disc brake assemblies and 8.6 million discs per annum.
3W brake assembly volume to double from 0.6 million to 1.2 million units per annum by end of 2026.
New SMT line at Sambhajinagar for ABS ECUs and BMS, installation expected June 2026. Chennai die-casting plant to add a 1,600-ton die casting machine.
AURIC Shendra: US EV OEM SOP June 2026, JLR July-August 2026. Solar actuators to start H2 FY27 from new Sanand building. Driveshaft business to cross ₹100 crores in FY27.
demand_pricing: Domestic 2W sales in Q4 rose 25.4% YoY per SIAM, with scooters up 37.1% and motorcycles up 19.8%.
FY26 India order wins were ₹1,596 crores (₹1,579 crores new business), with 4W and non-auto about ₹743 crores. Q4 wins were ₹316 crores.

Pass-through is the main issue: aluminium alloy and oil and gas costs rose sharply from March and April 2026. Customers are being asked for spot increases; some OEMs have confirmed while others are pending.
Europe operates on a quarterly price reset based on prior-quarter averages, so the impact is mainly a margin-percentage effect (denominator). Management says there is no material risk.
Management claims it grew faster than peers in FY26: Bajaj +16.1% vs Bajaj 11.6%, Honda +16.9% vs 7.9%, Royal Enfield +32.7% vs 23.9%, TVS +29.1% vs 21.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-time price impact in Q4 revenue, standalone or Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 RMC rose ₹160 crores (66.82% of revenue vs 65.3%), including ₹73.7 crores of non-pass-through aluminium and steel costs and ₹31.3 crores of outsourcing costs. Prior-year Q4 had about ₹25 crores of one-time gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ABS revenue trajectory with dual-channel SOP?
qa_highlights.answer: About 280,000 single-channel ABS units in FY26. Growth of 100-150% expected in FY27. The 12 lakh unit line will not be fully used initially.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for the greenfield plants and US EV OEM and JLR exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidkin alloy wheels reach peak in Q3-early Q4 FY27 (~₹600 crores p.a.). AURIC Shendra SOP for US EV OEM in June 2026 and JLR in July-August 2026, with FY27 revenue target above ₹200 crores. Battery pack SOP late May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company set up manufacturing in the US or Europe given high European energy costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said customers want China-plus-one sourcing from India, so growth will come from AURIC Shendra, which has 11 acres plus 24 acres available for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin headwinds behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 will still be volatile given rising oil, gas and alloy prices. It hopes the war ends next month, expects normalisation after that, and sees better numbers from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What edge does Endurance have in battery packs and BMS, given OEM backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited in-house patented busbar design and fully automatic lines for packs. It said very few players exist in pack and BMS. Management also said the pack solution was developed in-house and is for one OEM only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stöferle order book and European growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Stöferle brought about €7 million of new business from Magna and BMW. Stöferle's annual run rate at acquisition was about €70-80 million. Excluding Stöferle, Q4 Europe grew 7.4% and FY26 grew 2%.

rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell about 2 points to 10.5% as RMC rose to 70% of sales from 66%; management expects ~0.5% price increase from 1 October plus 0.5-0.6% commodity benefit, cutting RMC about 0.6% absolute in Q3, though part of the pass-through is still only agreed by some customers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ABS capacity rises to 1.54 million units per annum by Q4 FY27 (about 70% booked by Bajaj and Royal Enfield), the Chennai disc brake plant has SOP in March 2027, and the aluminium forging fifth press SOPs in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 order wins of ₹748 crore (excluding Bajaj), with cumulative wins of ₹6,372 crore since FY22 of which ₹3,798 crore is still to be realised; India EV sales rose 185% YoY to ₹229 crore; no explicit volume % guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already raised to about ₹1,100 crore standalone and ₹1,250 crore consolidated for FY27 (vs ~₹800 crore in FY26), with the new projects being built out; utilisation level was not disclosed, so a fresh announcement is probable rather than certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Maharashtra PSI incentive rises to ₹858 crore total with ₹75 crore booked in H1 and about ₹50 crore expected in H2 FY27, and Maxwell's margin is targeted to turn double-digit in FY28, but no revenue or margin guidance raise was made.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone RMC is at 70% of sales (vs 66%) and the Q3 RMC reduction depends on pass-through that only some customers agreed to, while management expects steel prices to rise; greenfield plants carry about a 0.5% negative PBT margin drag in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Battery pack SOP ramp for a leading 2W OEM completes in Q3 FY27, two PV OEM battery pack nominations start Q1-Q2 FY28, and the Sanand solar actuator SOP is in Q4 FY27 with US solar SOP in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Proprietary 4W and non-auto SOP ramp to FY31
rows.why: Targets are 4W SOPs of ₹100 crore in FY28 rising to ₹800 crore in FY31, non-auto SOP of ₹250 crore in FY28 rising to ₹650 crore by FY31, and proprietary 4W above ₹1,500 crore by FY31, though management says this is not achievable within two years.

rows.label: EU import caps and local-content rules
rows.why: A 350,000-unit cap on Chinese plug-in and mild hybrid imports starts 1 December 2026 and duties on Chinese BEVs apply, which management says could lift European volumes, but the impact is not quantified.

rows.label: Maxwell double-digit EBITDA margin
rows.why: Maxwell revenue reached ₹85 crore in Q2 (+94% YoY) and PAT has been positive for consecutive quarters, with management targeting double-digit EBITDA margin in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on order flow, EV and non-auto diversification, and the Q3 margin recovery, but cautious on battery pack margins and non-auto targets, and analysts pushed on price pass-through and the timing of the proprietary 4W ramp.

540173|2026-03.headline: PNB Housing Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores; FY27 guidance is loan book above INR 1 lakh crore and ROA 2.4-2.5%.
540173|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 36% YoY and 50% QoQ to INR 9,355 crores, with retail disbursements up 32% YoY to INR 9,020 crores. PAT rose 19% YoY to INR 656 crores in Q4 and 18% to INR 2,291 crores for FY26, helped by negative credit cost of 45 bps from write-off pool recoveries. Spread compressed 10 bps QoQ to 2.12% on lower incremental yields and balance transfer pressure in Prime, while reported NIM rose 6 bps to 3.69%. Management guided that yields have bottomed out, with FY27 retail loan growth of 18-20%, NIM of 3.55-3.65% and ROA of 2.4-2.5%.

+13% YoY; opex to ATA 1.05% FY26, 1.08% Q4

segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 34% YoY in Q4. Segment share of retail loan book rose with affordable plus emerging at 40% of retail book (37% a year earlier).

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 43% YoY in Q4 despite yield pressure from rate cuts. Management says Prime disbursement largely replenishes runoff; Prime loan growth is about 9%.

segments.name: Corporate

ROA guided at 2.4-2.5% for FY27.

Non-housing share of the book at 32.4% vs 30.6% in Q3; PBC retail home loans at 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the spread fall while NIM rose, and will the ROA gap normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said the divergence is a methodology difference (daily spread convention vs monthly NIM averaging) and should normalise from next quarter, with NIM in a 5-10 bps range of current trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost is built into the 2.4-2.5% ROA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said credit cost is expected to remain negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with write-off pool recoveries continuing; mix shift to emerging, affordable and corporate should support NIM over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did affordable disbursements weaken and is it linked to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said affordable disbursements rebounded in Q4, mid-year challenges were temporary and fixed, and quality is not the reason; Prime disbursement reflects replenishment of runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What early bounce and stress indicators are visible for April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April bounce rates are similar to March, with no significant jump; a one-off government-employee EMI bounce was cleared the next day.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident yields have bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said no repo change in recent months, so balance transfer outflows should restrict, supporting yield; BT out improved from Q3 to Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR 335 crore corporate disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one case in FY26 was about INR 360-370 crores, primarily in Mumbai; focus is on reputed builders in about seven or eight top cities, with corporate at about 3% of book in FY27.

risks_watch: Yield recovery depends on balance transfer outflows staying restricted and on no further rate cuts; management also flagged possible upside in market rates.
Credit cost is negative because of write-off pool recoveries (about INR 500 crores corporate and INR 325 crores retail remaining); normalisation could weigh on ROA.
Opex grew 13% and the full cost of 35 Q4 branches will flow into FY27; opex to ATA target 1-1.1%.
Cost of borrowing: management expects only stable to 5-10 bps improvement; a rating upgrade is being pursued as a lever.
Geopolitical and crude-oil risk could affect inflation, rates and asset quality, though management sees no early stress as of mid-April.
Prime 30+ DPD on a like-for-like basis is 2.72% (investor presentation figure of 3.31% includes Stage-2 SICR accounts).

540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.

NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.

Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit cost turn positive in H2, and what ROA path follows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE upgrade is done; ICRA and CRISIL pending. CFO said at least about 10 bps reduction in cost of borrowing should come through; some fresh borrowing already at better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

Disbursement realisation under cheque-realisation accounting: management expects the transition to flow through over about two months, so Q2 reported figures depend on timing of realisations.

Going forward, we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year.

540173|2026-09.headline: PNB Housing Q2 FY27 disbursements rose 60% YoY to INR 9,609 crore and spread widened to 2.43%, aided by a one-off; loan book up 19% YoY to INR 95,079 crore.

GNPA improved to 0.91% from 0.95% in Q1, and a INR 75 crore write-off recovery produced negative credit cost of 19 bps. The company was upgraded to AAA by CRISIL, taking all four domestic agencies to AAA, and management expects a phased benefit to borrowing costs.

financial_highlights.change: +60% YoY, includes INR 838 crore pool buyout
+20% YoY from INR 217 crore; opex to ATA 1.03%
includes INR 75 crore write-off recovery; about 11 bps excluding it

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off charge from the legacy corporate account and how is it accounted for?

qa_highlights.question: What is the sensitivity of cost of borrowing and margins to a 50 bps repo hike?

qa_highlights.question: Is rate-hike-driven demand softening, and how are competitors pricing?

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised credit cost?

qa_highlights.answer: INR100-125 crore goes to the digital platform, up to INR75 crore to the gold loan stake, and the balance to MSME and digital lending growth plus general corporate purposes. Management said no proceeds will go to repay lenders, since repayments come from the portfolio.

qa_highlights.answer: AUM rose from INR290-294 crore at March 2026 to INR610 crore, with growth from new borrowers, including INR125 crore in digital disbursement. Management projects INR2,000 crore in FY28 and INR3,000 crore in FY29.

540180|2026-03.headline: Varun Beverages Q1 CY2026 revenue rose 18.1% to Rs 65,742 mn and EBITDA 21% to Rs 15,289 mn on 16.3% volume growth.
540180|2026-03.overview: Consolidated volumes grew 16.3% to 363.4 mn cases, with India up 14.4% and international up 21.4%, after a weak prior-year summer hit by rains. Consolidated realisation per case rose 1.6% on favourable currency in international markets, while India realisation fell 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points. EBITDA margin expanded 55 bps to 23.3% and PAT rose 20.1% to Rs 8,787 mn, though depreciation (+30.9%) and finance cost (+18%) rose on new plants and the Twizza acquisition. Management said it is covered on packaging and raw materials for the current quarter and holds about 6 months of inventory internationally, with the crude-linked cost risk flagged for later quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume up 14.4%; realisation down 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points; India EBITDA margin up 112 bps on operating efficiencies and gross margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume up 21.4%, with management saying all international markets grew double digits except Morocco; Twizza (South Africa) acquired via BevCo at EV ZAR 2,053 mn.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: CSD 73.6% of volume, non-carbonated beverages 7.5%, packaged water 18.9%; low/no-sugar products about 63% of consolidated volume. Dairy growing about 60% with realisation near 3x normal; Tropicana PET above 100% growth.

segments.name: Snacks / food distribution (Africa)
segments.commentary: Q1 snack foods revenue Rs 112 cr vs Rs 52 cr in Q1 CY25; Zimbabwe plant commissioned end of last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 demand to be better than Q1 if weather holds; said first month of summer 'looks very good'.
India raw material cover is complete for this quarter and partial for next; international inventory about 6 months, so near-term impact described as zero to a couple of points.
Gasoline/transport cost increases expected to be absorbed by reducing discounts and efficiency gains; no major P&L impact expected if volumes hold.
India capex for CY26 expected below Rs 500-600 cr, with only one plant planned.
Management expects double-digit growth in India for the next 5-10 years and international growth not below double digits absent external shocks.
Expects about 500,000 new outlets to be added in CY26 on a base of about 4 mn outlets.
Crickley Dairy acquisition (EV about ZAR 238 mn incl. working capital) subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: India capex for CY26 to be under Rs 500-600 cr, with only about one new plant; existing capacity seen sufficient to deliver up to 50% growth without new capacity.

Four plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya) have stabilised; management says it is no longer opening smaller plants and cost of production in larger plants is about half that of smaller ones.
Twizza revenue about Rs 800 cr (last full year), acquisition price about Rs 1,140 cr; Crickley Dairy revenue about Rs 160 cr; combined about Rs 1,000 cr. Margins not yet guided.
Typical plant payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE, per management.
Aluminium cans are under 2% of sales; cans tied up above that level, though shortage in the industry.
demand_pricing: Management says the summer season is strong after a weak prior year, with May and June the key months; April end was 'not great'.
Industry chilling equipment additions of about 1 mn units per year (about 0.5 mn from Campa, Coke and VBL combined plus 0.4-0.5 mn own coolers by outlets).
Rs 10 price point used selectively, under 2% of total volume, to retain distributors.
Competitors (B-brands, water players) have cut discounts rather than raise prices, per management; PET and can shortages affecting the whole industry.
Ad-Rush (Rs 60 mid-priced energy drink) performing well above plan; can shortage constraining supply. Sting Classic launched in cans and PET (April), with early response described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the near-term impact of higher oil prices on packaging and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: International raw materials impact practically zero to a couple of points given about 6 months inventory; India has minor impact for this quarter and some for next, offset by lower discounts and cost cuts. Transport cost cannot be stocked but is absorbable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India realisation improve to -1.5% from -4% last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation through new launches and dairy growth of about 60% (realisation near 3x normal) helped, along with lower discounting and efficiency; Rs 10 price points are used selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company placed on aluminium cans and PET supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cans are under 2% of sales and tied up above that requirement; shortage is industry-wide and customers may switch to PET or glass.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2-year CAGR slowdown in India a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 6-8% figure, citing a 23% average CAGR historically; said last year was an exceptional weather-hit year and growth should stay double-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin hit if crude stays high for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds 6 months inventory and expects competitors to take price increases or absorb the hit first; does not expect to take a hit itself.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upsizing from 250 ml to 400 ml adding consumption, and is India margin affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption is rising both in litres and in units; full-quarter upsizing effects already absorbed by volumes and plant efficiency, with minor upsides to be absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plant payback and utilisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE; higher utilisation is helping as larger lines (1,000 bottles per minute vs 200) replace old high-cost plants.

risks_watch: Crude-linked input cost (PET, gasoline, transport) and aluminium can shortage could pressure margins from Q2 if discounts cannot be cut further.
India realisation may fall further (management said it 'might even become lower') with discounting and pack upsizing.
Weather risk: management says the season depends on rains and any abnormal rain could hurt volumes; prior-year weather hit was severe.
Integration of Twizza and Crickley Dairy: margins not yet disclosed; Crickley subject to regulatory approvals.
Finance cost and depreciation growth (+18% and +30.9%) will weigh on PAT growth relative to EBITDA.
540180|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and summer trends, with an assertive tone on cost cover. Management was evasive on specifics such as Twizza/Crickley margins, future price increases and competitor share, and pushed back on the analyst's 2-year CAGR framing.
key_quotes: We are completely covered for this quarter, and we are partly covered for the next quarter also.
We think other people will blink before we blink, we have to wait and see.
Normally we work on a 3-4 year payback. 30% RoCE.
Water is like a commodity, you can increase your sales as much as you want by offering discounts, which we are not in the game of and that is why we can sustain our margins.

rows.why: Sting Classic launched in cans and PET in April with a strong early response, Ad-Rush (Rs 60) is running well above plan, and dairy is growing about 60%, though no further launch dates were given.

rows.why: Twizza (acquired at about Rs 1,140 cr, last-year revenue about Rs 800 cr) is already consolidated and Crickley (about ZAR 238 mn, revenue about Rs 160 cr) awaits regulatory approval, adding roughly Rs 1,000 cr combined revenue with margins not yet guided.

rows.why: Management says gasoline and transport increases will be absorbed by cutting discounts and efficiency gains, with no major P&L impact if volumes hold; international inventory covers about 6 months.

540180|2026-06.headline: VBL Q2 CY2026 revenue rose 20.4% to Rs 84,512.3 mn and EBITDA 17.2% to Rs 23,430.4 mn, with India volume up 14.4%.
540180|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales volume grew 19.8% to 466.7 million cases in the quarter, with net revenue up 20.4% year-on-year. India volume grew 14.4%, with growth of about 20% or more in every month since March except April, which was roughly flat due to El Nino-driven rain. International volumes rose 38.4%, including 11.8 million cases from the newly consolidated Twizza business in South Africa. EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, while India margin improved 38 bps. Management also extended the PepsiCo bottling licence to April 2049 and announced the Calpis tie-up with Asahi and the Devyani Kenya acquisition.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (net of excise and GST)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value), cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 14.4% in Q2 with 20%+ monthly growth from March except April (about flat). India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps on operating efficiencies, partly offset by higher transport and distribution costs. Low-sugar/no-sugar products were about 73% of consolidated volume in H1.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume rose 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa; ex-Twizza growth was above 25%. Management said all African markets are growing except Zambia, which is small and slower. Twizza operates at lower margins, which diluted group EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Value-added dairy (VAD) and Nimbooz
segments.commentary: Management said VAD is growing above 40% and Nimbooz above 30% for the company, about 3x-4x the overall business. Growth figures were given only as ranges, with no absolute values.

segments.name: Food distribution and manufacturing in Africa
segments.commentary: Management said this business is growing about 50%. No absolute figures or targets were given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India growth of at least 20% month-on-month after June, with July tracking the same trend.
Management said India can keep growing in double digits despite a stronger competitive field from Campa and Coca-Cola, and argued the industry is growing about 20%.

Raw material costs have risen with the West Asia crisis. Part of the increase is booked in Q2 under average costing, and the balance will hit Q3. Management said the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.
Management said EBITDA margins can be maintained even in a high-crude year and would improve once the conflicts ease.
Energy drink labels must drop the word 'energy' within 90 days, per the regulator's guidance. Management said volumes are returning to STING as new labels roll out.
Management will not scale Rs 10 pricing for now, as it is not profitable for the company, unless monthly growth falls below 20%.
capex_capacity: H1 net capitalised capex of ~Rs 9,500 mn: ~Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India including a value-added dairy line at Supa, ~Rs 1,000 mn for a snack plant in Zimbabwe, and ~Rs 4,000 mn for market infrastructure (visi-coolers, glass bottles, pallets, vehicles).
Capital work-in-progress of ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026, mainly South Africa expansion and a CSD line in Kenya.
Inorganic capex of Rs 11,314 mn for the Twizza Limited acquisition in South Africa.
Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) business acquisition agreed, giving a ready go-to-market for CSDs and energy drinks in Kenya.
Twizza in South Africa helped overcome capacity constraints, with the company strengthening its manufacturing and route-to-market footprint there.
demand_pricing: India Q2 volume +14.4%, with April about flat due to heavy rain. May seasonality has shifted (it used to be about 15% of business before 2025), and management says non-weather months show high double-digit growth.
Rs 10 price point: management said it has not scaled it up because it is not profitable and the company is growing 20%+ without it. Some markets are pushing Rs 10 packs, but the mix is small.
Pack changes: the company is upsizing and downsizing packs by market. Management said volume is reported on an 8-ounce basis, and realisation per 8-ounce case and gross margin are said to be stable.
Competition: Campa Cola is expanding at Rs 10 and Rs 20 price points, and management said the Rs 20 gap has narrowed. The 400 ml Rs 20 pack is driving recruitment.
GST cuts: management said the impact on dairy, water and soda was minimal. Some prices were held despite geopolitical cost pressure.
Management declined to give market share data, saying it does not track share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to scale the Rs 10 price point, and how much of the April weakness was rain versus competition from Campa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not scaling Rs 10 because it is unprofitable. It said India is growing 20%+ month-on-month outside April, which was hit by El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into alcobev in India, and is it bidding for Bira?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only looking at possible new categories and is not bidding for Bira. Prathmesh Mishra was hired for the group, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: Can India grow at low double digits given stronger competitors and a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ravi Jaipuria said H1 India growth was 14.4% and July is continuing at the same trend, so double-digit growth looks achievable. Varun Jaipuria said weather, not demand, was holding back growth in months without rain.

qa_highlights.question: Up to what crude level can margins be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are maintainable even in a worse geopolitical year and that margins cannot get worse once conflicts ease. It did not give a crude threshold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the energy drink labelling change on STING?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June and July saw a temporary dip as volume moved to CSD. Volumes are returning as new labels roll out, and the regulator gave 90 days to remove the word 'energy'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Calpis tie-up extend to other Asahi brands or other categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current focus is stabilising Calpis. Dairy is a core category, and no decision has been made on RTD tea or coffee.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from the West Asia crisis: part of the cost is in Q2 under average costing, and the balance hits Q3.
Monsoon and El Nino weather volatility, which hurt April and shifted the seasonal pattern of May.
Lower Twizza margins, which pulled group EBITDA margin down 76 bps; further integration and dilution is possible.
Energy drink labelling change, with a 90-day compliance deadline. Some volume shifted to CSD in June-July.
Rising competitive intensity from Campa Cola's Rs 10 and Rs 20 packs and Coca-Cola, which could pressure India volume and pricing.
Net debt of ~Rs 3,730 mn at consolidated level after the Twizza acquisition.

540180|2026-09.headline: VBL Q3 CY2026 revenue rose 33.2% to Rs 66,076 mn, with gross margin down 334 bps to 53.1% on packaging cost inflation.
540180|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.2% YoY to Rs 66,076 mn and EBITDA rose 25.1% to Rs 14,267 mn, with EBITDA margin at 21.6% (down 140 bps). Volume growth was 28.7% consolidated, with India at 22.5% and international at 39.9%. Gross margin fell 334 bps to 53.1% as packaging inflation from the geopolitical conflict (around 300 bps) and a surge in lower-margin preform and cap sales (about 100 bps in India) weighed. Management said gross margin has likely troughed at current prices, and it announced an interim dividend of Rs 0.50 per share and a KIVA Spirits entry into alcobev/RTD.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 22.5% in Q3; realisation per case rose 0.5%. EBITDA margin was broadly stable YoY in 9M CY2026 despite input cost pressure. Low/no-sugar share rose to 88% from 44% a year ago.

segments.name: International (Africa)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 39.9% in Q3, with realisation up on South Africa pricing and FX. International gross margin pressure was about 272 bps versus about 300 bps in India. Twizza merged with BevCo effective 1 Aug 2026.

segments.name: Product mix (volume, Q3)
segments.commentary: CSD 73.3%, juice-based drinks 4.8%, packaged water 21.9% of sales volume. Non-beverage sales (preforms, caps) in India rose about 104%.

guidance_outlook: Management said gross margin has broadly troughed in Q3 CY2026 at current price trends, barring new macro surprises.
Upside to margins could come from price-pack architecture changes, following the Sting pack downsize from 300 ml to 250 ml.
Management said more than half of the 3-4% gross margin impact has been mitigated through cost reductions.
International capex is about USD 90-100 mn; India capex is about Rs 1,000 crore, including a greenfield plant at Suratgarh, Rajasthan and a PET line. CY2026 capex is complete.
Management plans to add about 100,000 outlets a year from the current 4.2 mn, and is aggressively planning numeric and weighted distribution for CY2027.
Calpis launch is planned for December-January, with a broader marketing calendar around late February or March.
capex_capacity: Capacity is full in most African markets; Morocco capacity is short ahead of its season and new lines are planned in Morocco, Zimbabwe and DRC.
South Africa and DRC seasons run November to January with plants at full speed; Twizza gives enough South African capacity this year.
Zimbabwe has a capacity gap that Zambia will partly cover from this month, and more capacity is being added next year.
rPET is about 25% of PET needs via in-house backward integration; the next rPET plant is expected to be operational within 1-2 quarters.
Capex across India and international markets is roughly Rs 1,000 crore and USD 90 mn respectively.
demand_pricing: India volume growth is 22.5%, and 9M India growth is about 16-17%; management said volume growth has been positive since May.
No list-price increase on CSD in Q3; realisation gains came from mix, premium launches (Ad Rush, Evervess mixers), calibrated discounting and price-pack architecture.

Sting pack reduced from 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June to offset raw-material costs. Energy category volumes were hit by an FSSAI labelling ruling; management estimated negativity at about 25% mid-quarter and said Sting is now recovering.
Rs 10 price point is about 0.2-0.3% of volume; management will not push it because unit economics do not work at 150 ml.
Africa: Mondelez exclusive distribution agreement in Zimbabwe (Mondelez has about USD 11 mn existing business there). Kenya beverage operations started with BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ.
Management said October is still in progress and declined to comment on October trends.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for gross margins next quarter and March quarter, and split of packaging, sugar and non-beverage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the packaging cost hit applies from purchases after the war began around 28 Feb; the company was covered for one quarter. It said the sugar impact was offset by low/no-sugar mix, and the 3-4% gross margin impact is more than half mitigated.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 gross margin the trough?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, broadly, at present price trends, with upside from price-pack changes. The pace of roll-down to other packs will determine that upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sugar or packaging price increase on CSD, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: No CSD price increase was taken in Q3; the only pack change was Sting 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the crude/PET cost increase is in the P&L?

540203|2026-03.headline: Sheela Foam Q4 FY26 consolidated core EBITDA rose 90% YoY to INR121 crore at an 11.5% margin, with first-ever dividend of 20% recommended.
540203|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,050 crore, and FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR3,821 crore, with management citing record foam production, top line and EBITDA. Core EBITDA for FY26 was INR414 crore (10.8% margin, up 261 bps), and consolidated PAT was INR92 crore in Q4 (about 7x YoY) and INR161 crore for FY26. Net debt fell INR156 crore in FY26, and the Board recommended a first-ever 20% dividend. Management flagged raw material (TDI, polyol) volatility from the Middle East conflict, saying prices were 25-35% higher on average, and that pass-through has largely been taken.

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Australia/Spain margin gain sustainable, and how much of it is inventory benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR27 lakh capex plus INR20-22 lakh working capital per store, with 42 operational of a 50-store target; about INR25 crore for another 50 COCO stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 96-97% complete, operating units cut to 12 from 21, and roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the remainder on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furlenco store rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: TDI/polyol (65-70% of COGS) swung roughly +40% to -20%; management expects volatility for at least a couple of months, possibly to October-November, so gross margin recovery timing is uncertain.

Overseas margin sustainability: Australia and Spain margins (12.8% and 14.7%) were helped by longer-held low-cost inventory and lower frequency of price changes; management expects moderation as India recovers and inventory normalises by Q2.

Volume recovery: standalone India volume grew about 6% against double-digit growth last year; management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27 and strongest volumes in Q3 and Q4, contingent on volatility subsiding.

Synergy and capex execution: about INR40 crore synergy pending the machine installation (full impact expected Q3); COCO rollout of 50 stores at about INR50 lakh each (~INR25 crore) and Furlenco shop-in-shop target of 100 stores from about 40-50.

540203|2026-09.headline: Sheela Foam Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% to INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA flat at INR87 crore (8.4% margin) as brand spend and raw-material inflation absorbed the gains.
540203|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR1,045 crore, the first time quarterly revenue crossed INR1,000 crore. Operating EBITDA was INR87 crore (8.4% margin), flat YoY, while reported EBITDA was INR83 crore after a one-off INR7 crore provision against an Australian customer. PAT was INR46 crore versus INR10 crore last year, helped by operations, lower finance cost and depreciation. Management said raw-material inflation (polyol up 65%, TDI up 33% since mid-February) and a larger Great Sleepwell Festival spend compressed margins, and that absolute profit was held. Furlenco became a subsidiary from 1 October 2026 and will be consolidated line by line from Q3.

Net debt: existing Sheela Foam consolidated about INR600 crore currently, expected INR500-550 crore by year-end; with Furlenco (net debt about INR250 crore) total about INR800 crore. FY28 debt reduction about INR200 crore per annum from free cash flow of INR150-200 crore.
Gross margin unit economics designed for 42%+; current gross margin about 38%.
Furlenco listing may be proposed for next year; value unlock still under consideration.
capex_capacity: Furlenco accounted for as subsidiary from 1 October 2026: 43% fully diluted stake but about 35% held on converted-equity basis; line-by-line consolidation from Q3 with minority interest deducted.
Furlenco now buys its furniture assets (previously leased); manufactures about 20-30% in-house and outsources the rest; ROCE about 25%.
Sheela Foam is developing a support-layer technology to launch products below INR10,000 price point at mid-segment margins, and a new U2O product to refill vacated INR8,000-9,000 price band.
Sleepwell and Kurlon beds and recliners launched online via Furlenco back-end; store rollout to follow.
Australian and Spanish businesses onboarding new customers, with volumes expected from H2.
demand_pricing: Raw materials: crude up about 50%; polyol up 65% and TDI up 33% since mid-February 2026; prices rising INR10-20 every 15 days at peak.
Management passed on increases multiple times; mattress prices up about 25% and foam about 35-40% since the conflict began. Mattress entry price moved from under INR10,000 to INR11,000-12,000.
Festive season moved from late September (Q2) to October (Q3), shifting demand; management said market picked up in September and October.
Gross margin about 38% versus historical 40-42%; management estimated INR15-20 crore of EBITDA was forgone from the margin trade-off in Q2.
Management estimates about 15-20% of global TDI capacity wiped out (war and European closures), with polyol somewhat less; the main constraint is logistics rather than capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup and outlook of other income (INR22 crore over past two quarters)?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income includes returns on about INR110 crore of investments (10-12% p.a.) plus asset sale gains or revaluation items; expected to run at about INR10 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the INR5,000 crore revenue and INR600 crore EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a pro forma run-rate: existing Sheela Foam about INR4,300-4,400 crore revenue and INR400-450 crore EBITDA, plus Furlenco about INR500-600 crore revenue and INR200 crore EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 EBITDA margin compressed, and how much was marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-16 crore extra advertising spend in Q2 versus plan; other expenses up INR8 crore YoY and INR15 crore QoQ; about INR8 crore of employee cost rise was FX translation of Australia and Spain, with yearly increments of 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 13-15% EBITDA margin target for next year still be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was on track before the war but is difficult now; achievable if raw-material costs normalise, with margin recovery of 2-3 points possible.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be reported by channel for the Sleepwell brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split volumes by channel, saying it views the brand as omnichannel and looks at overall brand growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Australian provision impact results?
qa_highlights.answer: A 38% haircut on receivables from A.H. Beard in administration cost about INR7 crore, booked across Q1 and Q2; management said it will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Mattress volume outlook for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Depends on the Middle East situation; if raw-material costs stay high, management will keep protecting margins at the cost of some volume; if they flatten or soften, growth should follow.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidation accounting and minority interest after Furlenco became a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation is at the converted-equity share (about 35%) under accounting standards, moving to 100% line-by-line with minority interest deducted; fully diluted stake is about 43%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR600 crore currently, expected INR500-550 crore by year-end excluding Furlenco; Furlenco net debt about INR250 crore; FY28 free cash flow of INR150-200 crore to reduce debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why are tax cash inflows showing INR33 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Amortisation of deferred tax assets from the Kurlon merger's tax-amortisable intangibles, plus a refund from revised returns for years after the October 2023 merger; management expects about INR150 crore of such benefit over one to two years.

risks_watch: Raw-material volatility: polyol, TDI and crude moves tied to Middle East disruption and Hormuz logistics; management said pricing relief depends on the Hormuz situation.
Margin trade-off: gross margin about 38% vs 40-42% historical; volume loss risk from repeated price hikes and consumer affordability limits.
U2O and sub-INR10,000 volumes: management is depending on new technology products to recover the vacated price band.
Furlenco consolidation and minority interest: complexity from 35% converted vs 43% diluted stake; listing and value-unlock timeline unclear.
Furlenco is capital-intensive (asset-based rental); management said net debt will not reduce there and it will draw cash to fund growth above 30%.
Australia (A.H. Beard) and Spain customer-acquisition costs weighed on Q2 margins; the Spain volume ramp is expected from H2.
key_quotes: With the strength of the brands, we've had the advantage of being able to pass these increases on to the market and eventually to the consumer.
So we had to provide those INR7 crores between the first and the second quarter.
If it prevails like this, I be lieve it's difficult to achieve, but if it normalizes, we will try to achieve it.
So we would suggest that we also look at it from the perspective of the overall brand and not through the channels from which it is sold.
But as far as payback or IRR is concerned, you understand that this is a competitive -- competition sensitive industry and those type of KPIs cannot be disclosed.

540205|2026-03.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.
540205|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR2,672 crore and PAT grew 11% to INR117 crore, with EBITDA at INR228 crore (8.5% margin) and gross margin at 15.6%. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 28% and same-store sales growth of 18%, though gross margin (16%) and EBITDA margin (8.1%) were lower than the prior year. Management said H2 is now as important as H1, reflecting a shift away from a seasonal model. Store count reached 207 across four states, with Chhattisgarh entered and Madhya Pradesh planned this year. Inventory was built up to about INR840 crore ahead of anticipated OEM supply constraints and BEE-driven price increases.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Largest market at 74% of Q4 FY26 revenue and 75% of FY26 revenue; 118 stores across 38 districts.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: 14% of Q4 and 13% of FY26 revenue; 53 stores covering 30 of 75 districts, with most new stores opened in Feb-Mar 2026 and contributing less than a full year.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Mobiles and laptops together exceed 25% of sales; ASP of mobiles rose about 20% in Q4, diluting gross margin. Small appliances grew about 50%, per analyst; cooling products (ACs, coolers, refrigerators) underperformed due to weak summer.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal store guidance; it cites about 25 stores when asked, and has added over 30 stores a year for the last 3-5 years.
Madhya Pradesh entry is on track for this financial year; Chhattisgarh and UP to be scaled up.
Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.
Management cites an 8% to 10% EBITDA margin range as its endeavour, with 9% as a central target, but declined to give a timeline.
April 2026 described as very robust; May started colder but is expected to normalise into a normal summer.
No equity raise planned this financial year; internal accruals and working capital borrowings are expected to suffice.
capex_capacity: Store base reached 207 at March 31, 2026, after 102 stores were added in the last three years versus 105 in the prior 23-24 years.
Stores take 9 to 12 months to break even, per management.
Inventory of about INR840 crore held at end Q4 FY26, built ahead of OEM supply uncertainty (gas shortages linked to a Gulf conflict) and BEE-driven price increases of about 8% to 10%.
Plans to scale UP and Chhattisgarh while deepening Bihar and Jharkhand; a neighbouring state, previously held back by political uncertainty, is now being considered.
demand_pricing: Weak summer and extended rains hit H1; Q1 FY26 revenue grew 6% and H1 grew 11%. Q3 grew 28%, driven by festive demand.
Historically Q1 and Q2 contributed 55% to 60% of annual sales; management says this is now shifting towards a more balanced full-year model.
Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.
Management said OEMs bear the burden of unsold inventory and do not take returns; they help liquidate stock before new billing.
Real estate slowdown seen in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad has not yet affected Bihar, UP or Jharkhand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will high inventory give a competitive and margin advantage over peers in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on peers' inventory and said it holds inventory as per its own strategy and historical levels, not to profit from price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 100 bps YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to weak cooling-product sales in H1 and a Q4 surge in low-margin mobiles (ASP up about 20%) and laptops (ASP up 8-10%), which together exceed 25% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to brand ambassador onboarding, UP expansion, and variable costs such as freight, card commissions and dealer discounts that rise with the 18% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose state-wise margins, saying it aims to bring other states up to Bihar's level over time without sacrificing sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance given; management cited 25 stores when pressed and said it expects to keep beating its informal targets.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline and pointed to an 8% to 10% margin range, with 9% as the central target, while not compromising sales growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward mobiles and laptops, whose ASPs are rising.
Q4 inventory build (about INR840 crore) exposes the company to price-cut and demand risk if the summer underperforms; May started colder than normal.
Cash conversion: management declined to guide on OCF/EBITDA, saying it depends on inventory and working capital.
Finance cost implies about 12.8-13% on average debt per analyst, but this includes lease liability interest; the bank borrowing rate was not disclosed.
Most UP stores opened in the last months of FY26, so UP contribution and unit economics are not yet visible on a full-year basis.
Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.
540205|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand momentum and the all-season model, but evasive on specifics: management declined to disclose state-wise margins, peer inventory, store targets, cash flow guidance and margin timelines.
key_quotes: I'm truly delighted to give the comfort to our investors and stakeholders that your company is now an all-weather, all-season company.
We do not give a guidance because we are always ahead of the guidance.
So it's not necessary that whenever there is a hike in price that comes as a profit to us.
I cannot give you a guidance on that. But our endeavor, we always give a guidance of between 8% to 10% of margin.

rows.why: Management gives no formal revenue or margin guidance and declined to give timelines, so no formal upgrade is signalled.

rows.why: Management said it is on track to enter Madhya Pradesh this financial year, with Chhattisgarh (3 stores, 2 of 33 districts) and UP being scaled up.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, April demand and the all-season model, but evasive on state-wise margins, peer inventory, store targets, cash-flow guidance and margin timelines; analysts pressed on the 100 bps gross margin fall and the 50% rise in other expenses.

540205|2026-09.headline: Aditya Vision Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.1% YoY to Rs 586.23 crore and PAT 45.2% to Rs 18.47 crore, with October demand described as slow.
540205|2026-09.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue up 27.3% to Rs 1,778.91 crore and same-store sales growth at 18%. Gross margin expanded 125 bps to 16.3%, but management attributed only about 75-80 bps of the quarter's margin gain to price hikes and guided normalised gross margin at 15-15.5%. Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali. The store network reached 214, with new entries into Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal, and the company guided to about 230-235 stores by FY27 end.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Contributed about 73% of Q2 revenue across all 38 districts, with 120 stores.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 15% of Q2 revenue from 56 stores across 32 of 75 districts.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of Q2 revenue from 33 stores across 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 1% of Q2 revenue from five stores across three of 33 districts; newly entered state.

guidance_outlook: Normalised gross margin guided at around 15%-15.5% at constant prices; price-driven gains are not built into guidance.
EBITDA margin guided at 8%-10% on an annual basis; management said margin will moderate as price-driven gross margin gains fade, with the impact that year roughly equal to the gross margin effect.
Store count expected at around 230, possibly up to 235, by end FY27, and about 35 more stores in FY28 (about 270 total).
Chhattisgarh: 9-10 more stores planned. Madhya Pradesh: about 3 stores shortly and 15-17 in the coming year. West Bengal: at least 15 stores, with 40-50 stores possible over about four years.
New-store breakeven expected in about one year; management said new-state margin dilution would be offset by maturing older stores.
capex_capacity: Capex per store is about Rs 90 lakh, up from earlier levels due to inflation over the last 1.5 years.
Capex in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh could be 10%-15% higher than in core markets due to freight and vendor logistics costs, depending on store size.
Retail footprint expanded 18.3% to about 9.51 lakh sq ft as of September 30, 2026.
Entered West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh in the period (as of October 2026); two West Bengal stores opened and two more in progress.
Cluster-based expansion leverages logistics, vendor relationships and brand recall.
demand_pricing: Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up as Dhanteras and Diwali approach.
Q2 growth was led by AC, followed by mobile and refrigerators, helped by an extended summer.
Around 75-80 bps of the Q2 gross margin gain came from OEM price increases; the rest came from normal trading.
H1 same-store sales growth was 18%, versus 2% in H1 FY26 when unseasonal rains hurt footfall.
West Bengal competitors include Reliance and Croma, plus a local chain, which are stronger in metros than in peripheral districts; the company is targeting border districts near Bihar first.
Headwinds cited: West Asia conflict, energy disruption, higher crude prices, Bihar floods and cyclone, and rising staples and cooking gas prices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 125 bps gross margin expansion in Q2, and is the full-year margin guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes contributed about 75-80 bps and normal trading the rest; normalised gross margin guidance stays at 15%-15.5% at constant prices.

qa_highlights.question: How has demand been in October and was the festive season delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales have been slow so far, but expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali; it could not predict the outcome precisely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did indirect expenses rise sharply YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said OPEX was controlled and at a similar sales ratio. Higher indirect costs reflect financing, credit card, CMS and freight costs scaling with sales, plus about 30 stores added in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and breakeven for new stores in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 90 lakh per store, with breakeven expected in about one year; management said it was too early to guide on the new states specifically.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8th Pay Commission be a demand driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be a strong tailwind through higher discretionary spending, but depends on the macro environment.

risks_watch: Slow October demand; whether the festive pick-up materialises before Dhanteras and Diwali.
Normalisation of gross margin after price-driven gains, which management said will moderate EBITDA margin in the same proportion.
Indirect expense growth (Rs 17 crore to about Rs 28 crore YoY in Q2 per analyst, +64%) as the company enters new states.
Breakeven and margin dilution in new states (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal) and competition from national chains in West Bengal.
Inventory at Rs 865 crore (up from Rs 840 crore since March 2026) and borrowings of Rs 293 crore (up YoY from prior-year levels).

key_quotes: Our normal guidance will remain the same, around 15%-15.5%.
We always give guidance of 8%-10%, and we are very confident that we will be able to achieve it.
In fact, demand has been slow, let me put it like this.

rows.why: H1 same-store sales grew 18% and revenue 27.3%, but October demand is slow and growth depends on a Dhanteras and Diwali pick-up, with store additions of about 7.5% (214 to ~230) supporting volume.

rows.why: Capex is already set at about Rs 90 lakh per store and store plans for Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal are specified, so further store-level capex is committed; no utilisation figure was given, so no new capex programme is confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue growth guide, price-driven margin gains are excluded from guidance, and October demand is slow with festive pick-up only expected, not confirmed.
